body.text: || namo buddhaya |
body.translated_text: || Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>. |

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ sarvatra na vidyate svabhāvaś cet /
children.translated_text: If the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of all things is not found anywhere,

children.text: tvadvacanam asvabhāvaṃ na nivartayitum svabhāvam alaṃ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: then your statement, being without intrinsic nature, is not capable of negating intrinsic nature. || NagVv 1 ||

body.text: yadi sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ hetau pratyayeṣu ca hetupratyayasāmagrāñ ca pṛthak ca yatra sarvatra svabhāvo na vidyata iti kṛtvā śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti | na hi bije hetubhūte 'ṅkuro sti | na pṛthivyaptejovāyvādinām ekekasmin pratyayasaṃjñite | na pratyayeṣu samagreṣu na hetupratyayeṣu samagreṣu na hetupratyayasāmagrāṃ na hetupratyayavinirmuktaḥ pṛthag eva vā | yasmād atra svabhāvo nāsti tasmān niḥsvabhāvo 'ṅkuraḥ | yasmān niḥsvabhāvaḥ tasmāt śūnyaḥ | yathā cāyam aṅkuro niḥsvabhāvo niḥsvabhāvāc ca śūnyaḥ tathā sarvabhāvā niḥsvabhāvatvāc chūnya iti |
body.translated_text: [Opponent's commentary:] If the intrinsic nature of all things is not found in the cause, in the conditions, in the aggregate of cause and conditions, or separately anywhere—and therefore all things are empty—for there is no sprout in the seed which is the cause; not in each of the conditions designated as earth, water, fire, air, and so forth; not in the conditions collectively; not in the cause and conditions collectively; not apart from the aggregate of cause and conditions; not separately and independently—since intrinsic nature does not exist in any of these, the sprout is without intrinsic nature. Since it is without intrinsic nature, it is empty. And just as this sprout is without intrinsic nature and empty because of being without intrinsic nature, so all things are empty because of being without intrinsic nature.

body.text: atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ | yady evaṃ tavāpi vacanaṃ yady etac chūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tad api śūnyaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tad api hetau nāsti | mahābhūteṣu saṃprayukteṣu viprayukteṣu vā pratyayeṣu nāsti | uraḥkaṇthoṣṭhajihvādantamūlatālunāsikāmūrdhaprabhṛtiṣu yan naivobhayasāmagryām asti | hetupratyayasamagrīvinirmuktaṃ pṛthag eva vā nāsti | yasmād atra sarvatra nāsti | tasmān niḥsvabhāvaṃ | yasmān niḥsvabhāvaṃ | tasmāc chūnyaṃ | tasmād anena sarvabhāvasvabhāvavyavartanam aśakyaṃ kartuṃ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃn | na hy asadagninā dagdhaṃ | nāpy asatā śāstreṇa śakyaṃ chettuṃ | nāsatībhir atbhiḥ śakyaṃ kledayitum evam asattā vacanena śakyaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvapratiṣedhaḥ kartuṃ na śakyaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvo nivartayituṃ | tatra yad uktaṃ sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ pratiṣidhaḥ sarvatra bhāvasvabhāvo vinivartata iti | tan na ||
body.translated_text: Here we say: If so, then your statement too—'all things are empty'—is also empty. For what reason? Because it too does not exist in the cause. It does not exist in the great elements combined or separated as conditions; not in the chest, throat, lips, tongue, teeth-roots, palate, nose, head, and the rest—not in the aggregate of both. It does not exist independently apart from the aggregate of cause and conditions. Since it does not exist anywhere here, therefore it is without intrinsic nature. Since it is without intrinsic nature, therefore it is empty. Therefore, it is impossible by this to negate the intrinsic nature of all things. For what reason? A non-existent fire does not burn. Nor can a non-existent weapon cut. Nor can non-existent waters moisten. Similarly, by a non-existent statement the intrinsic nature of all things cannot be negated; the intrinsic nature of all things cannot be dispelled. Therefore, what was said—that the intrinsic nature of all things is negated and dispelled everywhere—that is not valid.

children.text: atha sasvabhāvam etad vākyaṃ pūrvā hata pratijñā te /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, this statement possesses intrinsic nature, your former thesis is destroyed;

children.text: vaiṣamikatvaṃ tasmin viśeṣahetuś ca vaktavyaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: there is inconsistency therein, and a distinguishing reason must be stated. || NagVv 2 ||

body.text: athāpi manyase mā bhūd eṣa doṣa iti sasvabhāvam etad vākyaṃ | sasvabhāvatvāc cāśūnyaṃ | tasmād anena sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvo vinivarta iti ||
body.translated_text: And if you think, 'Let this defect not arise,' and so this statement possesses intrinsic nature—and because it possesses intrinsic nature, it is non-empty—therefore, by this, the intrinsic nature of all things is negated, and the intrinsic nature of all things is dispelled—

body.text: atra brūmaḥ | yā hi te pratijñā śūnyāḥ svabhāvā iti | hatā śā || kiñcānyat sarvabhāvāntargatañ ca tadvacanam | kasmāt sarvabhāveṣu tvadvacanam aśūnyaṃ yenāśūnyatvāt sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ || evaṃ ṣaṭkoṭiko vādaḥ prasaktaḥ | sa punaḥ katham iti |
body.translated_text: Here we say: Your thesis—'all things are empty in intrinsic nature'—is destroyed. Moreover, that statement is included among all things. Why should your statement alone, among all things, be non-empty, and by virtue of this non-emptiness negate the intrinsic nature of all things? Thus a six-pointed argument (<s>ṣaṭkoṭika vāda</s>) follows. And how is that?

body.text: hanta cet punaḥ śūnyāḥ sarvahhāvās tena tvadvacanaṃ śūnyam sarvabhāvāntargatatvāt tvadvacanasya | tena śūnyena pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ | tatra yaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ śūnyāḥ sarvabhāva iti anupapannaḥ | 1 | upapannaś cet punaḥ śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti pratiṣedhas tena tvadvacanaśūnyatvād anena pratiṣedho anupapannaḥ | 2 | atha śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvās tvadvacanañ cāśūnyaḥ yena pratiṣedhas tena tvadvacanaṃ sarvatrāsaṃgṛhītaṃ |
body.translated_text: Consider: If all things are empty, then your statement too is empty, being included among all things. Since it is empty, a negation is untenable. Thus the negation 'all things are empty' is untenable. (1) And if the negation 'all things are empty' is tenable, then since your statement is empty, by this the negation is untenable. (2) Now if all things are empty but your statement is non-empty, by which the negation is made, then your statement is not included anywhere among all things.

body.text: tatra dṛṣṭāntavirodhaḥ | 3 | sarvatra cet punaḥ gṛhītaṃ tvadvacanaṃ sarvabhāvāś ca śūnyāḥ | tena tad api śūnyaṃ śūnyatvād anena nāsti pratiṣedhaḥ | 4 | atha śūnyam asti vānena pratiṣedhaḥ śūnyaḥ sarvabhāvā iti tena śūnyāpi sarvabhāvāḥ kāryakriyāsamarthā samarthabhaveyuḥ | na caitad iṣṭaṃ | 5 | atha śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ na ca kāryaṃ kriyāsamarthaṃ bhavaṃti mā bhūt dṛṣṭāntavirodha iti kṛtvā śūnyena tvadvacanena sarvabhāvāsvabhāvo pratiṣedho nopapanna iti | 6 |
body.translated_text: In that case, there is a counter-example contradiction. (3) And if your statement is included among all things and all things are empty, then that too is empty, and because of its emptiness there is no negation by it. (4) Now if, even though empty, there is a negation by it—'all things are empty'—then even though all things are empty, they should be capable of efficacious activity. But that is not desired. (5) And if all things are empty and yet are not capable of efficacious activity—let there not be a counter-example contradiction—then by your empty statement, the negation of the intrinsic nature of all things is untenable. (6)

body.text: kiñcānyat | evaṃ tadastitvāt vaiṣamikatvaprasaṅgaḥ | kiñcit śūnyaṃ kiñcid aśūnyam iti | tasmiṃś ca vaisamikatve viśeṣahetur vaktavyaḥ | yena hi viśeṣahetunā kiñcit śūnyaṃ kiñcid aśūnyaṃ syāt | sa ca nopadiṣṭo hetuḥ | tatra yad uktaṃ śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, from the existence of that [non-empty statement], there follows the undesirable consequence of inconsistency—'some things are empty, some are non-empty.' And regarding that inconsistency, a distinguishing reason must be stated—by which distinguishing reason some things would be empty and some non-empty. And no such reason has been indicated. Therefore, what was said—'all things are empty'—that is not valid.

body.text: kiñcānyat
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: mā śabdavad ity etat syāt te buddhir na caitad upapannam /
children.translated_text: 'Let it be like the prohibition of sound'—this may be your thought; but this is not tenable;

children.text: śabdenātra satā bhaviṣyato vāraṇaṃ tasya || 3 ||
children.translated_text: for here the prevention of the future [sound] is by an existent sound. || NagVv 3 ||

body.text: syāt te buddhiḥ yathā nāma kaścit brūyāt mā śabdaṃ kārṣīr mā śabdaṃ kārṣīr iti | tena ca śabdena vyāvartanaṃ kriyate | evam eva śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti | śūnyena vacanena sarvatā sarvabhāvasvabhāvavyāvartanaṃ kriyata iti |
body.translated_text: You may think: Just as someone might say, 'Don't make a sound! Don't make a sound!'—and by that sound a prevention is effected—in the same way, 'all things are empty,' and by an empty statement the intrinsic nature of all things everywhere is dispelled.

body.text: atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ | etad apy anupapannaṃ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | satā hy atra śabdena hy atra bhaviṣyataḥ śabdasya pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate | na punar iha bhavataḥ satā vacanena sarvabhāvasvabhāvapratiṣedhaḥ kriyate | tava hi matena vacanam apy asat | sarvabhāvasvabhāvo 'py asat | tasmād ayaṃ mā śabdavad iti viṣayopanyāso 'sann iti ||
body.translated_text: Here we say: This too is untenable. For what reason? Because here it is by an existent sound that the prohibition of a future sound is effected. But in your case, the negation of the intrinsic nature of all things is not effected by an existent statement. For according to your view, the statement too is non-existent; the intrinsic nature of all things too is non-existent. Therefore, this presentation of a subject matter—'let it be like the prohibition of sound'—is non-existent.

body.text: kiñca
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: pratipratiṣedhyo 'py evam iti mataṃ bhavet tad asad eva /
children.translated_text: If you think that the counter-negation too is untenable in the same way, that is simply false;

children.text: evaṃ tava pratijña lakṣaṇato dūṣyate na mama || 4 ||
children.translated_text: for thus your thesis is refuted by its own definition, not mine. || NagVv 4 ||

body.text: syāt te buddhiḥ pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyo 'py anenaiva kalpenānupapannaḥ | tatra yad bhavān sarvabhāvasvabhāvapratiṣedhaśūcanaṃ pratiṣedhayati | tad anupapannam iti |
body.translated_text: You may think: The counter-negation too is untenable by this very same method. That is, what you negate—the indication of the negation of the intrinsic nature of all things—that counter-negation is untenable.

body.text: atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ | etad aśabdena sad eva | kasmāt tava ca hi pratijñālakṣaṇaprāptam etan na mama bhavān iha bravīti | śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti nāhaṃ | tasmāt tvatpratijñān na(?)payāmi | pūrvakaḥ pakṣo na mama | tatra yad uktaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyo 'py evaṃ matam iti | upapannaṃm iti || tan na |
body.translated_text: Here we say: This assertion is wrong. For what reason? Because what follows from the definition of your thesis does not apply to me. You say, 'All things are empty,' not I. Therefore I challenge your thesis. The prior position is not mine. Therefore, what was said—'the counter-negation too is untenable in the same way'—that is not valid.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: pratyakṣeṇa hi tāvad yady upalabhya vinivartayasi bhāvān /
children.translated_text: If indeed you negate things having apprehended them through perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>),

children.text: tan nāsti pratyakṣaṃ bhāvā yenopalabhyante || 5 ||
children.translated_text: that perception by which things are apprehended does not exist. || NagVv 5 ||

body.text: yadi pratyakṣataḥ sarvabhāvān upalabhya bhavān nivartayati śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti | tad anupapannaṃ | kasmāt pratyakṣam api hi pramāṇaṃ svabhāvāntargatatvāt śūnyaṃ | yo 'pi sarvabhāvān upalabhate so 'pi śūnyas tasmāt pratyakṣeṇa pramāṇena nopalambhabhāvo anupalabdhasya ca pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ śūnyaḥ sarvabhāvā iti | tad anupapannaṃ
body.translated_text: If you negate all things having apprehended them through perception—'all things are empty'—that is untenable. For what reason? Because even perception as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge), being included among all things, is empty. And whoever apprehends all things, he too is empty. Therefore, there is no apprehension of things by the means of knowledge called perception; and the negation of what is not apprehended is untenable—'all things are empty.' That is untenable.

body.text: syāt te buddhiḥ | anumānenāgamenopānena vā sarvabhāvān upalabhya sarvabhāvavyāvartanaṃ kriyata iti ||
body.translated_text: You may think: By inference (<s>anumāna</s>), scripture (<s>āgama</s>), or analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), having apprehended all things, the dispelling of all things is effected.

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here we say:

children.text: anumānaṃ pratyuktaṃ pratyakṣeṇāgamopamāne ca /
children.translated_text: Inference is answered just as perception was; and likewise scripture and analogy.

children.text: anumānāgamasādhyā ye 'rthā dṛṣṭāntasādhyāś ca || 6 ||
children.translated_text: And those objects established by inference, scripture, and example [are also answered]. || NagVv 6 ||

body.text: anumānam apy upamānāgamāś ca pratyakṣeṇa pramāṇena pratyuktāḥ | yathā hi pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ śūnyaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ śūnyatvāt | evam anumānamopamāgamāpi śūnyāḥ | sarvabhāvānāṃ śūnyatvāt | ye 'py anumānasādhyārthā āgamasādhyā upamānasādhyāś ca | te 'pi śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ śūnyatvāt* anumānopamānāgamaiś ca yo 'pi bhāvān upalabhate so 'pi śūnyaḥ tasmāt bbāvānām upalambhābhāvo 'nupalabdhānāñ ca svabhāvapratiṣedhānupapattiḥ | tatra yad uktaṃ śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti | tan na ||
body.translated_text: Inference, analogy, and scripture are also answered just as the <s>pramāṇa</s> of perception was. For just as perception is empty because of all things being empty, so too are inference, analogy, and scripture empty, because of all things being empty. And those objects established by inference, established by scripture, and established by analogy—they too are empty, because of all things being empty. And whoever apprehends things through inference, analogy, and scripture, he too is empty. Therefore, there is no apprehension of things; and the negation of the intrinsic nature of things that are not apprehended is untenable. Therefore, what was said—'all things are empty'—that is not valid.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmāvasthavidaś ca manyante /
children.translated_text: Those who know the conditions of <s>dharmas</s> consider the intrinsic nature of beings

children.text: kuśalaṃ janasvabhāvaṃ śeṣeṣv apy eṣa viniyogaḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: to be wholesome with respect to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; and this same application holds for the remaining types as well. || NagVv 7 ||

body.text: iha dharmāvasthāvido manyante kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām ekonaviṃśaṃ śataṃ | tadyathā ekadeśo vijñānasya vedanāyāḥ | saṃjñāyāś cetanāyāḥ | sparśasya manasikārasya chandasyādhimokṣasya vīryasya smṛteḥ samādheḥ prajñāyā upekṣāyāḥ prayogasya saṃprayogasya prāpto 'dhyāśayasya prativirateḥ vyavasāyā autsukyasya | unmūrdhe utsāhasya avyārtyasya vasitāyāḥ pratipatter avipratīsārasya dhṛter adhyavasāyasya | anaukṣekasya ananumūḍhyanutsārasya | prāpaṇāyāḥ praṇidheḥ madasya viṣayānāṃ viprayogasya | aniryāṇikatāyā utsādasya | sthiter anityatāyāḥ samarthāgatasya jarāyāḥ paridrāsyatārateḥ | vitarkānāṃ prīteḥ pramādasya aprasrabdheḥ | vyavahāratāyāḥ | prekṣupratikūlasya pradakṣiṇagrāhasya vaiśāradyagauravasya citrīkārasya
body.translated_text: [The opponent:] Here, those who know the states of <s>dharmas</s> maintain that there are one hundred and nineteen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Namely: a portion of consciousness, of feeling, of perception, of volition, of contact, of attention, of desire, of resolve, of vigor, of mindfulness, of concentration, of wisdom, of equanimity, of application, of association, of what is attained, of higher intention, of abstinence, of determination, of zeal, of upward rising, of enthusiasm, of non-injury, of mastery, of understanding, of non-regret, of firmness, of resolution, of non-contempt, of non-delusion, of non-reversal, of conveyance, of aspiration, of intoxication, of disengagement from sense-objects, of non-soteriological nature, of suppression, of stability, of impermanence, of what comes appropriately, of old age, of weariness and impatience, of thought-patterns, of joy, of heedlessness, of non-tranquility, of conduct,

body.text: bhakter abhakteḥ suśrūṣāyāḥ sādarasyānādarasya prasrabdheḥ | hāsasya vācaḥ viṣpandanāyāḥ siddhasyāprasādasya aprasrabdheḥ vyavahāratāyaḥ | dākṣyasya sauratyasya vipratisārasya śokasya | upāyāsāyas vītasya | apradakṣiṇagrāhasya saṃepasya saṃvarāṇāṃ pariśuddher adhyāśayasya rūpasyeti | śraddhā hrīr ārjavam avañcanaṃ | upasama acāmala saprasādamārdavaṃ pratisaṃkhyānaṃ nirveda 'paridāhaḥ | amada alobha adoṣa amoha asarvat* apratiniḥsargaḥ vibhava apatrayā apariśucchadanaṃ mānanaṃ kāruṇyaṃ maitrī adīnatādaritamari.(d)ha + + nupanāhaḥ alī cetaso paryādānaṃ kṣāntiḥ | vyavasadu āsaurakyam iti bhāgānvayaṃ | puṇyaṃ | asaṃjñisamāpattiḥ | nairyāṇikatāsarvajñatāsaṃskṛtā dharmāḥ ity ekonaviṃśaṃ śataṃ kuśalānāṃ kuśalaḥ svabhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: of devotion, of non-devotion, of obedience, of respect, of disrespect, of tranquility, of laughter, of speech, of trembling, of accomplishment, of displeasure, of non-tranquility, of conduct, of dexterity, of gentleness, of remorse, of grief, of distress, of freedom, of unfavorable reception, of restraint, of purity of restraints, of higher intention, of form — thus. Faith, modesty, rectitude, non-deception, calmness, purity, graciousness, gentleness, reflection, disenchantment, non-torment, non-intoxication, non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, non-attachment, non-relinquishment, prosperity, fearlessness, non-concealment, reverence, compassion, friendliness, non-despondency, firmness, non-resentment, non-seizure of mind, patience, determination, gentleness — thus by [their] component classification. Merit. The attainment of non-perception. Soteriological nature, omniscience, the unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> — thus [there are] one hundred and nineteen wholesome [dharmas]. Wholesome is [their] intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>).

body.text: tathākuśalānām akuśalaḥ svabhāvaḥ | nivṛttāvyākṛtaḥ | prakṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ prakṛtāvyākṛtaḥ | kāmoktānāṃ kāmoktaḥ | rūpoktānāṃ rūpoktaḥ | ārūpyoktānām ārūpyoktaḥ | anāśravāṇām anāśravaḥ | duḥkhoktānāṃ duḥkhoktaḥ | samudayoktānāṃ samudayoktaḥ | nirodhoktānāṃ nirodhoktaḥ | mārgoktānāṃ mārgoktaḥ | bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ bhāvanāprahātavyaḥ | aprahātavyānām aprahātavyaḥ | prahātavyānāṃ prahātavyaḥ | yasmād evam anekaprakāro dharmasvabhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ | tasmād iha yad uktaṃ | niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ niḥsvabhāvatvāt śūnya iti tan na |
body.translated_text: Likewise, the intrinsic nature of unwholesome [dharmas] is unwholesome. Of the ceased-undetermined [dharmas], [it is] ceased-undetermined. Of the naturally undetermined, naturally undetermined. Of those pertaining to the desire-realm, [it is] desire-realm. Of those pertaining to the form-realm, form-realm. Of those pertaining to the formless realm, formless-realm. Of those that are without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), without outflows. Of those pertaining to suffering, [it is] suffering-related. Of those pertaining to origination, origination-related. Of those pertaining to cessation, cessation-related. Of those pertaining to the path, path-related. Of those to be abandoned by cultivation, to-be-abandoned-by-cultivation. Of those not to be abandoned, not-to-be-abandoned. Of those to be abandoned, to-be-abandoned. Since in this way the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> has been seen to be of many kinds, therefore the statement made here — 'All entities lack intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) and are empty because of lacking intrinsic nature' — that is not [correct].

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nairyāṇikasvabhāvo dharmo nairyāṇikāś ca ye teṣāṃ /
children.translated_text: The intrinsic nature of a <s>dharma</s> that is soteriological (<s>nairyāṇika</s>) is soteriological, and those [dharmas] that are soteriological —

children.text: dharmāvasthoktānām eva ca nairyāṇikādīnāṃ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: and of the <s>dharmas</s> spoken of in [the system of] states of <s>dharmas</s>, the soteriological ones and so forth. // NagVv 8 //

body.text: iha ca dharmo 'vasthoktānāṃ nairyāṇikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ niryāṇikaḥ svabhāvaḥ | anairyāṇikānām anairyāṇikaḥ | bodhyaṅgikānāṃ bodhyaṅgikaḥ | abodhyaṅgikānām abodhyaṅgikaḥ | bodhipākṣikāṇāṃ bodhipākṣikaḥ | abodhipākṣikāṇām abodhipākṣikaḥ | evaṃ śeṣāṇāṃ tad yasmād evam anekaprakāro dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ | yasmād yad uktaṃ niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ | niḥsvabhāvatvāt śūnyā iti na ||
body.translated_text: And here, of the soteriological <s>dharmas</s> spoken of in [the system of] states of <s>dharmas</s>, the intrinsic nature is soteriological. Of the non-soteriological, it is non-soteriological. Of those conducive to awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgika</s>), it is conducive to awakening. Of those not conducive to awakening, not conducive to awakening. Of those on the side of awakening (<s>bodhipākṣika</s>), it is on the side of awakening. Of those not on the side of awakening, not on the side of awakening. Likewise for the rest. Since in this way the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> has been seen to be of many kinds — therefore, the statement 'All entities lack intrinsic nature and are empty because of lacking intrinsic nature' — that is not [correct].

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yadi ca na bhavet svabhāvo dharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāva ity evaṃ /
children.translated_text: If the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> did not exist — [if they are] 'lacking intrinsic nature' thus —

children.text: nāmāpi bhavet naivaṃ nāmāpi nirvastukan nāsti || 9 ||
children.translated_text: even the name would not exist in this way; a name too does not exist without a [corresponding] thing. // NagVv 9 //

body.text: yadi ca dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvo bhāvānāṃ svabhāvānāṃ sadbhāvāc cāśūnyaḥ sarvabhāvāḥ | tatra yad uktaṃ niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvā niḥsvabhāvatvāt śūnyā iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: If the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>, the intrinsic nature of entities, exists and [entities] are therefore non-empty — all entities [are non-empty]. In that regard, the statement 'All entities lack intrinsic nature and are empty because of lacking intrinsic nature' — that is not [correct].

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: atha vidyate svabhāvaḥ sa ca dharmāṇāṃ na vidyate tasmāt /
children.translated_text: Now, [suppose] intrinsic nature exists, but it does not pertain to <s>dharmas</s>; therefore

children.text: dharmair vinā svabhāvaḥ sa yasyāsti tad yuktam upadeṣṭum || 10 ||
children.translated_text: that intrinsic nature apart from <s>dharmas</s> — whose is it? It would be proper to indicate that. // NagVv 10 //

body.text: atha manyase mā bhūd avastukaṃ nāmeti kṛtvāsti svabhāvaḥ | sa punar dharmāṇāṃ na saṃbhavati | evaṃ dharmaśūnyatā ca niḥsvabhāvatvād dharmāṇāṃ siddhā bhaviṣyati | na ca nirvastukan nāmeti |
body.translated_text: [The opponent:] Now, if you think, 'Lest the name be without a [corresponding] thing, [let us say] intrinsic nature exists; but it does not belong to <s>dharmas</s>' — in this way, the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s>, being the essencelessness of <s>dharmas</s>, would be established; and the name would not be without a [corresponding] thing.

body.text: atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ | evaṃ kasyedānīṃ sa svabhāvo dharmavinirmuktasyārthasya tad yuktam upadeṣṭum arthaḥ | sa ca nopadiṣṭas tasmād yā kalpanāsti svabhāvo na punar dharmāṇām iti sā hīnā ||
body.translated_text: To this we [<s>Nāgārjuna</s>] say: In that case, whose is that intrinsic nature — of a thing devoid of <s>dharmas</s>? It would be proper to indicate that referent. But it has not been indicated. Therefore, the supposition that 'intrinsic nature exists but does not [belong to] <s>dharmas</s>' — that is defective.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: sata eva pratiṣedho nāsti ghaṭo geha ity ayaṃ yasmāt /
children.translated_text: Negation is only of what exists — 'There is no pot in the house' — since this

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ pratiṣedho yaṃ sataḥ svabhāvasya te tasmāt || 11 ||
children.translated_text: negation has been observed [to apply to] what exists, your [negation] is therefore of an existing intrinsic nature. // NagVv 11 //

body.text: iha ca sato 'rthasya pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate nāmataḥ | tadyathā nāsti ghaṭo geha iti | sato ghaṭasya pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate | nāsataḥ | evam eva nasti svabhāvo dharmāṇām iti | sataḥ svabhāvasya pratiṣedhaḥ prāpnoti nāmataḥ | tatra yad uktaṃ | niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ niḥsvabhāvatvāt śūnyā iti tan na || pratiṣedhasaṃbhavād eva hi sarvabhāvasvabhāvasvabhāvo 'pratiṣiddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, the negation of an existing thing is made nominally. For example, 'There is no pot in the house' — the negation is made of the existing pot, not of a non-existing [one]. In the same way, 'There is no intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>' — this negation necessarily applies to an existing intrinsic nature, nominally. In that regard, the statement 'All entities lack intrinsic nature and are empty because of lacking intrinsic nature' — that is not [correct]. For precisely because negation is possible, the intrinsic nature of the intrinsic nature of all entities is not negated.

children.text: atha nāsti sa svabhāvaḥ kin na pratiṣidhyate tvayānena /
children.translated_text: Now, if that intrinsic nature does not exist, what is it that is not being negated by you with this

children.text: vacanena rte vacanāt pratiṣedhaḥ sidhyate hy asataḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: statement? For negation of the non-existent is established without a statement. // NagVv 12 //

body.text: nāsty eva svabhāvā ity anena vacanena niḥsvabhāvā bhāvā iti kiṃ bhavatā pratiṣidhyate | asato hi vacād vinā siddhaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ | tadyathāgneḥ śaityasya | ayaṃ sthairyasya |
body.translated_text: 'There is absolutely no intrinsic nature' — by this statement, [you claim] that entities lack intrinsic nature. What then is being negated by you? For the negation of the non-existent is established without [any] statement. Just as [the negation of] coldness in fire, [and of] mobility in this [firmness].

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: bālānām iva mithyā mṛgatṛṣṇāyāṃ yathājalagrāhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as for children there is a false apprehension of water in a mirage,

children.text: evaṃ mithyāḥ grāhaḥ syāt te pratiṣidhyate hy asataḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: so too would your apprehension be false — for what is non-existent is [thereby] negated. // NagVv 13 //

body.text: syāt te buddhiḥ yathā bālānāṃ mṛgatṛṣṇāyāṃ mithyājalam iti grāho bhavati | nanu nirjalā sā mṛgatṛṣṇeti tatra paṇḍitajātīyena puruṣeṇocyate | tasya mithyāgrāhasya vinivartanārtham evan niḥsvabhāveṣu yaḥ svabhāvo grāhaḥ satvānāṃ tasya vyāvartanārthan niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvā ity ucyata iti ||
body.translated_text: [<s>Nāgārjuna</s> responds:] You might think: Just as children have the false apprehension 'There is water' in a mirage — for indeed that mirage is waterless, [as] is said by a person of the learned class for the purpose of removing that false apprehension — in the same way, with respect to [entities] lacking intrinsic nature, the apprehension of intrinsic nature by beings — for the purpose of removing that — it is said 'All entities lack intrinsic nature.'

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we [the opponent] say:

children.text: nanv evaṃ saty asti grāho grāhyañ ca tadgrahītā ca /
children.translated_text: But if so, there exists apprehension and the object of apprehension and the apprehender,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣedhā ceti ṣaṭkaṃ tat || 14 ||
children.translated_text: negation and the object of negation and the negators — thus a sixfold set. // NagVv 14 //

body.text: yady evaṃ nanv evaṃ saty asti tāvat satvānāṃ mithyāgrāhaḥ | asti grāhyaṃ santi satvā grahītāraḥ | asti pratiṣedhaḥ tasyāpi mithyāgrāhasyāsti pratiṣedhyaṃ yad idaṃ mithyāgrāhyaṃ nāma | santi pratiṣedhāro yuṣmadādayo 'sya mithyāgrāhasyeti siddhaṃ ṣaṭkam | ṣaṭkasyāsya prasiddhatvāt | yad uktaṃ śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: If so, then in that case there exists the false apprehension of beings; there exists the object of apprehension; there exist beings as apprehenders; there exists the negation of that false apprehension; there exists the object of negation, namely this false object of apprehension; and there exist the negators, such as yourselves, of this false apprehension — thus the sixfold set is established. Because this sixfold set is established, the statement 'All entities are empty' — that is not [correct].

children.text: atha naivāsti grāho na ca grāhyaṃ na ca grahītāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, if there is no apprehension, no object of apprehension, and no apprehenders,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣedhāro 'py ata na santi || 15 ||
children.translated_text: then negation, the object of negation, and the negators also do not exist. // NagVv 15 //

body.text: atha mā bhūd eṣa doṣa iti kṛtvā naiva grāho 'sti naiva grāhyaṃ na ca grahītāra iti | evaṃ sati yo 'sau grāhasya pratiṣedhaḥ niḥsvahhāvāḥ sarvabhāvā iti | so 'pi nāsti pratiṣedhyam api nāsti pratiṣedhāro 'pi na santi |
body.translated_text: Now, if — lest this fault [arise] — there is indeed no apprehension, no object of apprehension, and no apprehenders, then in that case, the negation of apprehension, namely 'All entities lack intrinsic nature,' also does not exist; the object of negation also does not exist; and the negators also do not exist.

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣedhārāaś ca yady uta na santi /
children.translated_text: If negation, the object of negation, and the negators do not exist,

children.text: siddhā hi sarvabhāvā yeṣām evaṃ svabhāvaś ca || 16 ||
children.translated_text: then all entities are established — as having intrinsic nature. // NagVv 16 //

body.text: yadi ca na pratiṣedho na pratiṣedhyaṃ na pratiṣeddhāraḥ santy apratisiddhāḥ sarvabhāvā asti ca sarvabhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: If there is no negation, no object of negation, and no negators, then all entities are unnegated, and intrinsic nature belongs to all entities.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: hetoḥ svato na siddhiḥ naiḥsvābhāvyāt kuto hi te hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: The proof (<s>hetu</s>) is not established on its own; since all [things] lack intrinsic nature, from where is your proof?

children.text: nirhetukasya siddhir na copapannāsya te 'rthasya || 17 ||
children.translated_text: And the establishment of this thesis of yours without a proof is not tenable. // NagVv 17 //

body.text: niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvā ity etasmin arthe te hetor asiddhiḥ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvād dhi sarvabhāvānāṃ śūnyatvān na tato hetuḥ | asati hetau nirhetukasyārthasya śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti kuta eva prasiddhiḥ || tatra yad uktaṃ śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: For the thesis 'All entities lack intrinsic nature,' your proof (<s>hetu</s>) is not established. For what reason? Because, since all entities are empty due to lacking intrinsic nature, there is no proof from that [emptiness]. In the absence of a proof, how indeed can the thesis 'All entities are empty' be established? Therefore, the statement 'All entities are empty' — that is not [correct].

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yadi cāhetoḥ siddhiḥ svabhāvavinivartanasya te bhavati /
children.translated_text: And if you hold that the establishment of the negation of intrinsic nature can be without a proof (<s>hetu</s>),

children.text: svābhāvyasyāstitvaṃ mamāpi nirhetukaṃ siddhaṃ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: the existence of intrinsic nature is also established for me without a cause. // NagVv 18 //

body.text: atha manyase nairhetukī siddhiḥ niḥsvabhāvatvasya bhāvānām iti | yathā tava svabhāvanirvartanaṃ nirhetukaṃ siddhaṃ | tathā mamāpi svabhāvasatbhāvo 'pi nirhetukaḥ siddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, if you think that the establishment of the lack of intrinsic nature of things is without a cause — then just as the production of intrinsic nature is established for you without a cause, so too for me, the existence of intrinsic nature is also established without a cause.

children.text: atha hetor astitvaṃ bhāvānaiḥsvābhāvyam ity anupapannam /
children.translated_text: Now, if the existence of a cause [is admitted], the lack of intrinsic nature of things is untenable.

children.text: loko naiḥsvabhāvyān na hi kaścana vidyate bhāvaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: In the world, because of the lack of intrinsic nature, no thing whatsoever exists. // NagVv 19 //

body.text: iha yadi hetor astitvaṃ manyase | niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tad anupapannaṃ || kiṃ karaṇaṃ | na hi loke niḥsvabhāvaḥ kaścid bhāvo 'sti ||
body.translated_text: Here, if you think there is the existence of a cause — [then the thesis] 'all things lack intrinsic nature' is untenable. For what reason? Because in the world, no thing exists that lacks intrinsic nature.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: pūrvaṃ cet pratiṣedhaḥ paścāt pratiṣedhyam iti na copapannam /
children.translated_text: If the negation [comes] first and the negated [thing comes] after — that too is not tenable;

children.text: yaś cānupapanno yugapac ca yataḥ svabhāvo 'san || 20 ||
children.translated_text: and [it is] untenable [if they are] simultaneous, since intrinsic nature is non-existent. // NagVv 20 //

body.text: iha pūrvaṃ cet pratiṣedhaḥ paścāc ca pratiṣedhyaṃ | niḥsvabhāvyaṃ nopapannaṃ | asati hi pratiṣedhye kasya pratiṣedhaḥ || atha paścāt pratiṣedhaḥ pūrvaṃ pratiṣedhyam iti ca nopapannaṃ | siddhe hi pratiṣedhye kiṃ pratiṣedhaḥ karoti | atha yugapatpratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhye tathāpi na pratiṣedhyaḥ pratiṣedhyasyārthasya kāraṇaṃ prati na pratiṣedhyaḥ | na pratiṣedhasya ca | yathā yugapadutpannayor goviṣāṇayoḥ naiva dakṣiṇaṃ savyasya kāraṇaṃ savyaṃ vā dakṣiṇasya gāraṇaṃ bhavatīti | tatra yad uktaṃ niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tan na |
body.translated_text: Here, if the negation [comes] first and the negated [thing comes] after, the lack of intrinsic nature is not tenable; for in the absence of the thing to be negated, what is the negation of? Now, if the negation [comes] after and the negated [thing comes] first — that too is not tenable; for when the negated [thing] is already established, what does the negation accomplish? Now, if the negation and the negated [thing are] simultaneous — even then, the negated is not [the cause of] the negation, for the negated thing is not [the cause] with respect to the negation, nor is [the negation the cause] of the negation. Just as, of two horns of a cow produced simultaneously, the right is not the cause of the left, nor is the left the cause of the right. Therefore, the statement 'all things lack intrinsic nature' is not [valid].

body.text: atrocyate | yat tāvad bhavatoktaṃ
body.translated_text: To this we say: As for what you have stated —

body.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ sarvatra na vidyate svabhāvaś cet |

children.text: tvadvacanam asvabhāvaṃ na nivartayituṃ svabhāvam alam iti | [1]
children.translated_text: your statement, being without intrinsic nature, is not capable of negating intrinsic nature' — [1]

body.translated_text: 'If the intrinsic nature of all things does not exist anywhere,

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we say:

children.text: hetupratyayasāmagrāṃ pṛthagbhāve 'pi madvaco na yadi /
children.translated_text: If my statement does not exist in the totality of causes and conditions, nor even when they are separate,

children.text: nanu śūnyatvaṃ siddhaṃ bhāvānām asvabhāvatvāt || 21 ||
children.translated_text: then surely <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is established, because of the lack of intrinsic nature of things. // NagVv 21 //

body.text: yadi madvaco hetau nāsti mahābhūteṣu saṃprayukteṣu viprayukteṣu vā pratyayeṣu nāsti | uraḥkaṇthojihvādantatālunāsikamūrdhaprabhṛtiṣu ya + + sāmagryām asti heṃpratyayasāmagrīṃ vinirmuktaṃ pṛthag vāsti | tasmān niḥsvabhāvā niḥsvabhāvatvāc chūnyaṃ | evaṃ | nanu śūnyatvaṃ siddhaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvād asya madīyavacasaḥ | yathā caitan madvacaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvāc chūnyaṃ | tathā sarvabhāvā niḥsvabhāvatvāc chūnyā iti | yad bhavatoktaṃ tvadīyavacasaḥ śūnyatvāt śūnyatā sarvabhāvānāṃ nopapadyata iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: If my statement does not exist in the cause — in the great elements whether conjoined or separated — nor in the conditions — the chest, throat, lips, teeth, palate, nose, head, and so forth — nor in the totality [of causes and conditions], nor separately apart from the totality of causes and conditions — therefore, it lacks intrinsic nature; because of lacking intrinsic nature, it is empty. Thus, surely <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is established, because of the lack of intrinsic nature of this statement of mine. And just as this statement of mine is empty because of lacking intrinsic nature, so too all things are empty because of lacking intrinsic nature. Therefore, what you have stated — 'because of the emptiness of your statement, the emptiness of all things is not tenable' — that is not so.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: yaś ca pratītya bhāvānāṃ śūnyateti taṃ brū + + /
children.translated_text: One who speaks of the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of things as dependent [origination]...

children.text: yas tu pratītyabhāvo bhavati hi tasyāsvabhāvatvaṃ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: that which arises dependently — its lack of intrinsic nature indeed obtains. // NagVv 22 //

body.text: śūnyatārthañ ca bhavān bhāvānām anavasamya śūnyatārtham ajñātvā pravṛtti upālambhaṃ vaktuṃ tvadvacanasya śūnyatvāt tvadvacanasya niḥsvabhāvatvād evaṃ tvadvacanena niḥsvabhāvena bhāvānāṃ svabhāvapratiṣedho nopapadyata iti | iha hi yaḥ pratītya bhavānāṃ bhāvaḥ sā śūnyatā | kasmān niḥsvabhāvatvāt | ye hi pratītyasamutpānnā bhāvās te sa sasvabhāvā bhavanti | svabhāvābhāvāt | tasmād dhetupratyayāpekṣatvāt | yadi hi svabhāvato bhāvā bhaveyuḥ | pratyākhyāyāpi hetupratyayāṃś ca bhaveyuḥ | na cevaṃ bhavanti | tasmān niḥsvabhāvāḥ niḥsvabhāvatvāc chūnyā ity abhidhīyante | evaṃ madīyam api vacanaṃ | pratītyasamutpannatvān niḥsvabhāvaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvāt śūnyam ity upapannaṃ |
body.translated_text: And you, without understanding the meaning of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of things, not knowing the meaning of emptiness, have proceeded to make the objection: 'Because of the emptiness of your statement, because of the lack of intrinsic nature of your statement, thus by your statement which lacks intrinsic nature, the negation of the intrinsic nature of things is not tenable.' Here, that which is the dependent arising of things — that is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). Why? Because of the lack of intrinsic nature. For things that are dependently arisen do not have intrinsic nature, because of the absence of intrinsic nature, because of being dependent on causes and conditions. For if things existed by their own nature, they would exist even after rejecting causes and conditions. But they do not exist in that way. Therefore, they lack intrinsic nature; because of lacking intrinsic nature, they are called 'empty.' Thus my statement too, being dependently arisen, lacks intrinsic nature; because of lacking intrinsic nature, it is empty — this is tenable.

body.text: yathā ca pratītyasamutpannatvāt svabhāvaśūnyāḥ | rathapaṭaghaṭādayaḥ sveṣu sveṣu kāryeṣu kāṣṭhāhaṇamṛttikaharaṇamadhūdakapayasāṃ dhāraṇā śītavātātapaparitrāṇaprabhṛtiṣu vartante | evam idaṃ madīyavacanaṃ pratyayasamutpannatvān niḥsvabhāvaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaprasādhanaṃ pratyayabhāvānāṃ vartate | tra yad uktaṃ | niḥsvabhavatvāt tvadīyavacanasya śūnyatvaṃ śūnyatvāt tasya ca tena sarvabhāvasvabhāvapratiṣedha upapannam iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: And just as chariots, cloths, pots, and the like, being empty of intrinsic nature because of being dependently arisen, function in their respective tasks — the carrying of wood, the conveying of earth, the holding of honey, water, and milk, the protection from cold, wind, and heat, and so forth — so too this statement of mine, lacking intrinsic nature because of being dependently arisen, functions to establish the lack of intrinsic nature of things. Therefore, what was stated — 'Because of the lack of intrinsic nature of your statement, because of its emptiness, the negation of the intrinsic nature of all things by it is not tenable' — that is not so.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: nirmitako nirmitakaṃ māyāpuruṣa svamāyayā sṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Just as a magically created [person] might negate another magically created [person], a magical man [might negate] one created by his own magic —

children.text: pratiṣedhayati yadvat pratiṣedho yaṃ tathaiva syāt || 23 ||
children.translated_text: the negation of that which is [to be negated] would be just like that. // NagVv 23 //

body.text: yathā nirmitakaḥ puruṣam abhyāpataṃ tu kaścid arthena vartamānaṃ pratiṣedhayet | māyākāreṇa vā sṛṣṭo māyāpurnṣo 'nyaṃ māyāpuruṣa samabhyava tan na kasminścid arthe vartamānaṃ pratiṣedhayet | tatra yo nirmitakaḥ puruṣaḥ pratiṣedhyate sa śūnyaḥ yaḥ pratiṣedhayati so 'pi māyāpuruṣaḥ śūnya evam eva madvacanena śūnyena sarvabhāvānāṃ svabhāvapratiṣedha upapannaḥ || tatra yad bhavatoktaṃ | śūnyatvāt tvadvacanasya sarvabhāvasvabhāvapratiṣedho nopapannam iti na tan na | ṣaṭkoṭiko vāda uktaḥ sa evaṃ pratisiddhaḥ naiva hy evaṃ sati na sarvabhāvāntargataṃ madvacanaṃ nāpy aśūnyaṃ nāpi sarvabhāvāśūnyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as a magically created person might negate another person approaching with some purpose; or a magical man created by a magician might encounter another magical man engaged in some purpose and negate him — there, the person who is negated is empty, and the one who negates, that magical man, is also empty — in exactly this way, the negation of the intrinsic nature of all things by my empty statement is tenable. Therefore, what you have stated — 'Because of the emptiness of your statement, the negation of the intrinsic nature of all things is not tenable' — that is not so. The six-pointed argument has been stated and thus refuted; for in this case, my statement is neither not included among all things, nor is it non-empty, nor are all things non-empty.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktam
body.translated_text: Now, as for what you have stated —

body.text:
atha sasvabhāvam etad vākyaṃ pūrvā hatā pratijñā te
vaiṣamikatvaṃ tasmin viśeṣahetuś ca vaktavya ity [2]
body.translated_text: 'If this statement of yours has intrinsic nature, your former thesis is defeated; there is inconsistency in that, and a special reason must be stated [for the exception]' — [2]

body.text: atrāpi brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this too we say:

children.text: na svābhāvikam etad vākyaṃ tasmān na vādahānir me /
children.translated_text: This statement is not [endowed] with intrinsic nature; therefore there is no defeat of my thesis.

children.text: nāsti ca vaiṣamikatvaṃ viśesahetuś ca na nigadyaḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: There is no inconsistency, and a special reason need not be stated. // NagVv 24 //

body.text: na tāvad etan mama vacanaṃ pratītyasamutpannatvāt svabhāvopapannaṃ yathā pūrvam uktaṃ | svabhāvānupapannatvāt śūnyaṃ | yasmāc ca idam api madvacanaṃ śūnyaṃ śeṣāpi sarvabhāvāḥ śūnyās tasmān nāsti vaiṣamikatvaṃ | yadi hi vayaṃ brūmaḥ | idaṃ vacanam aśūnyaṃ śeṣāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ śūnyā iti tato vaiṣamikatvaṃ | syān na caitad evaṃ tasmān na vaiṣamikatvaṃ | yasmāc ca vaiṣamikatvaṃ na saṃbhavati idaṃ vacanam aśūnyaṃ śeṣāḥ punaḥ sarvabhāvāḥ śūnyā iti | tasmād asmābhir viśeṣahetur api na vaktavyaḥ anena idaṃ vacanaṃ aśūnyaṃ sarvabhāvāḥ punaḥ śūnyā iti | tatra yad bhavatoktaṃ vādahānis te vaiṣamikatvaṃ ca viśeṣahetuś ca tvayā vaktavya iti tan na |
body.translated_text: This statement of mine, being dependently arisen, is not endowed with intrinsic nature, as was stated before. Because intrinsic nature is untenable, [it is] empty. And since this statement of mine too is empty, and all remaining things are also empty, therefore there is no inconsistency. For if we were to say 'this statement is non-empty, but all remaining things are empty,' then there would be inconsistency. But this is not so; therefore there is no inconsistency. And since inconsistency is not possible — [namely, that] 'this statement is non-empty, but all remaining things are empty' — therefore a special reason too need not be stated by us [to the effect that] 'by this [reason], this statement is non-empty, but all things are empty.' Therefore, what you have stated — 'there is defeat of your thesis, inconsistency, and a special reason must be stated by you' — that is not so.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now, as for what you have stated —

body.text: mā śabdavad ity etad asmāt te buddhir na caitad upapannaṃ |

children.text: śabdena hy atra satā bhaviṣyato vāraṇaṃ tasyeti | [3]
children.translated_text: for by an existent sound, there will be the prevention of that [sound]' — [3]

body.translated_text: 'Let it be like the [prohibition of] sound' — this notion of yours, but this is not tenable,

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we say:

children.text: mā śabdavad iti nāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto yas tvayā mamārahdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The example 'like sound' that you have adduced against me is not [applicable],

children.text: śabdena hi tac ca śabdasya vāraṇaṃ naidam eva caḥ || 25 ||
children.translated_text: for by sound there is [both] that [sound] and the prevention of sound — but this is not the same [as our case]. // NagVv 25 //

body.text: nāpy ayam asmākaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yathā kaścin mā śabdaṃ karṣīr iti bruvaṃ śabdam eva karoti śabdañ ca pratiṣedhayati | yadvat śūnyena vacanena śūnyatāṃ pratiṣedhayati | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | atra hi dṛṣṭānte śabdena śabdasya vyāvartanaṃ kriyate | na caitad evaṃ vayaṃ brūmaḥ | niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ niḥsvabhāvatvāt tad aśūnyām iti |
body.translated_text: This example is not [applicable] to our [position]. Just as someone saying 'Do not make a sound!' produces a sound while negating sound — [you say] similarly, by an empty statement one negates emptiness. For what reason? Because in this example, the prevention of sound is effected by sound. But we do not speak in this way — [we say] 'all things lack intrinsic nature because of the lack of intrinsic nature,' which is not the same [as that example].

body.text: kiṃ karaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: For what reason?

children.text: naiḥsvabhāvyānāṃ cen naiḥsvābhāvyena vāraṇaṃ yadi hi /
children.translated_text: If by the lack of intrinsic nature, the prevention of things lacking intrinsic nature were effected,

children.text: naiḥsvabhāvyanirvṛttau svabhāvyaṃ hi prasiddhaṃ syāt || 26 ||
children.translated_text: then, upon the negation of the lack of intrinsic nature, the possession of intrinsic nature would indeed be established. // NagVv 26 //

body.text: yathā mā śabdam iti śabdena śabdasya vyāvartanaṃ kriyate | evaṃ yadi naiḥsvabhāvyena vacanena naiḥsvabhāvyānāṃ vyāvartanaṃ kriyate tato 'yaṃ dṛṣṭāntopapannaḥ syāt | iha tu naiḥsvabhāvyena vacanena bhāvānāṃ svabhāvapratiṣedhaḥ kriyate | evaṃ yadi naiḥsvabhāvyena vacanena niḥsvabhāvānāṃ naiḥsvabhāvyapratiṣedhaḥ kriyate | naiḥsvabhavyapratiṣedhād eva sasvabhāvā bhaveyuḥ | sasvabhāvatvād aśūnyāḥ syuḥ | śūnyatāñ ca vayaṃ bhāvānām ācakṣmahe nāśūnyatām ity adṛṣṭānta evāyam iti |
body.translated_text: Just as by the [prohibition] 'Do not make a sound,' the prevention of sound is effected by sound — if in the same way the prevention of things lacking intrinsic nature were effected by a statement lacking intrinsic nature, then this example would be applicable. But here, by a statement lacking intrinsic nature, the negation of the intrinsic nature of things is effected. Thus, if by a statement lacking intrinsic nature, the negation of the lack of intrinsic nature of things lacking intrinsic nature were effected — then by the very negation of the lack of intrinsic nature, they would possess intrinsic nature; because of possessing intrinsic nature, they would be non-empty. But we declare the emptiness of things, not non-emptiness — therefore this is indeed a non-example.

children.text: atha vā nirmitakāyāṃ yathā striyāṃ striyam ity asatgrāham /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, just as a magically created [man] might dispel in someone the false apprehension 'It is a woman' regarding a magically created woman —

children.text: nirmitakaḥ pratihanyāt kasyacid evaṃ bhaved ettata || 27 ||
children.translated_text: in this way it could be for someone. // NagVv 27 //

body.text: atha vā kasyacit puruṣasya nirmitakāyāṃ striyāṃ svabhāvaśūnyāyāṃ paramārthataḥ striyam ity asadgrāhaḥ | syād eva tasyāṃ tenāsadgrāheṇa rāgam utpādayet | tad yathā tathāgatena vā tacchrāvakeṇa vā nirmitako nirmitaḥ syāt | tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena vā tathāgatasrāvakādhiṣṭhānena vā tasya tam asadgrāhaṃ vinivartayet | evam eva nirmitakopamena śūnyena vacanena nirmitakastrīsadṛśyeṣu niḥsvabhāveṣu yo 'yaṃ svabbāvagrāhaḥ sa nivartyate sa pratiṣidhyate | tasmād ayam atra dṛṣṭāntaḥ śūnyatāprasādhanaṃ pratyupapadyamāno netaraḥ |
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, some person might have a false apprehension 'It is a woman' regarding a magically created woman who is empty of intrinsic nature in the ultimate sense. He might indeed generate desire for her through that false apprehension. Then, just as a magical creation might be created by a <s>Tathāgata</s> or by a disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> or the empowerment of a disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, [that creation] might dispel his false apprehension. In exactly the same way, by a statement that is empty — like a magical creation — the apprehension of intrinsic nature in [entities] that are devoid of intrinsic nature, like the magically created woman, is turned away and negated. Therefore, this illustration here — as an establishment of emptiness — is fitting, not the other [interpretation].

children.text: atha vā sādhyasamo yaṃ hetur na hi vidyate dhvaneḥ sattā /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, the reason [you cite] is equal to what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>), for there is no real existence of sound;

children.text: saṃvyavahārañ ca vayaṃ nānabhyupagamya kathayāmaḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: and we do not speak without accepting conventional usage (<s>saṃvyavahāra</s>). // NagVv 28 //

body.text: mā śabdavad iti sādhyasama evāyaṃ hetuḥ | kasmāt sarvabhāvānāṃ naiḥsvabhāvyenāviśiṣṭatvāt | na hi tasya dhvaneḥ pratītyasamutpannatvāt | svabhavaṃ sattāḥ vidyate | tasyāḥ svabhāvasattāyāḥ avidyamānatvāt |
body.translated_text: [You said] 'Just as with sound' — but this reason is equal to what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>). Why? Because all entities are undifferentiated in their lack of intrinsic nature. For that sound, being dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), has no intrinsic existence. Since that intrinsic existence is non-existent,

body.text: yad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: what was stated —

body.text: śabdena hy atra sattā bhaviṣyato vāraṇaṃ tasyeti |
body.translated_text: 'For by the existence of sound there will be a prevention of that [emptiness]' —

body.text: tat vyāhanyate |
body.translated_text: that is contradicted.

body.text: api ca na vayaṃ vyavahārasatyaṃ pratyākhyāya vyavahārasatyam anabhyupagamya kathayāmaḥ | śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti | na hi vyavahārasatyam anāgamya śakyā dharmadeśanā kartuṃ |
body.translated_text: Moreover, we do not speak by rejecting conventional truth (<s>vyavahāra-satya</s>), by not accepting conventional truth, [when we say] 'All entities are empty.' For it is not possible to teach the <s>Dharma</s> without relying on conventional truth.

body.text: yathoktaṃ
body.translated_text: As it has been stated:

body.text: vyavahāram anāśritya paramārtho na deśyate |

children.text: paramārtham anāgamya nirvāṇaṃ nādhigamyata iti | [= MMK 24.18]
children.translated_text: without reaching the ultimate truth, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not attained.' [= MMK 24.10]

body.translated_text: 'Without relying on convention, the ultimate truth cannot be taught;

body.text: tasmān madvacanavat śūnyāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvānāñ ca niḥsvabhāvatvam ubhayathopapadyamānam iti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, like my statement, all entities are empty, and the lack of intrinsic nature of all entities is tenable in both ways.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now, as to what was further stated by you:

body.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyo 'py evam iti mataṃ bhavet tad asad eva |

children.text: evaṃ tava pratijñā lakṣaṇato dūṣyeta na mameti | [4]
children.translated_text: In this way, your thesis would be vitiated by [its own] defining characteristic, not mine.' [verse 4]

body.translated_text: '[You say] the negation itself is also negated — let that be your view; that is simply false.

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we say:

children.text: yadi kācana pratijñā tatra syān na me tat* eṣa me bhaved doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: If I had any thesis whatsoever, then this fault would be mine;

children.text: nāsti ca mama pratijñā tasmān naivāsti me doṣaḥ || 29 ||
children.translated_text: but I have no thesis — therefore I have no fault at all. // NagVv 29 //

body.text: yadi ca kācin mama pratijñā syāt tato mama pratijñālakṣaṇaprāptatvāt sa pūrvako doṣaḥ | yathā tvayoktaṃ bhāvāḥ tathā mama syān na ca mama kācid asti pratijñā | tasmāt sarvahhāveṣu śūnyeṣv atyantopaśānteṣu prakṛtivivikteṣu kutaḥ pratijñālakṣaṇaprāptiḥ kutaḥ pratijñālakṣaṇatāprāptikṛto doṣaḥ | tatra yat bhavatoktaṃ pratijñālakṣaṇaprāptatvāt tavaiva doṣa iti tan nāsti |
body.translated_text: If I had some thesis, then, by my thesis having attained the defining characteristic [of a thesis], that aforementioned fault would be mine — as you have stated, regarding entities. But I have no thesis whatsoever. Therefore, since all entities are empty, utterly quiescent, and isolated by nature — from where would there be the attainment of a defining characteristic of a thesis? From where would there be a fault arising from the attainment of a thesis-characteristic? In that regard, what you stated — that the fault belongs to me because of my thesis having a defining characteristic — that is not [correct].

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ
body.translated_text: Now, as to what was further stated by you:

body.text: pratyakṣeṇa hi tāvad yady upalabhya nivartayasi bhāvān

children.text: tan nāsti pratyakṣaṃ bhāvā yenopalabhyaṃta | [5]
children.translated_text: that perception through which entities would be apprehended does not exist.' [verse 5]

body.translated_text: 'If, to begin with, you negate entities after apprehending them through perception,

body.text: anumānaṃ pratyuktaṃ pratyakṣeṇāgamopamāne

children.text: cānumānāgamasādhyā ye 'rthā dṛṣṭāntasādhyāś ceti | [6]
children.translated_text: And the objects established by inference, scripture, and example [are also refuted].' [verse 6]

body.translated_text: 'Inference is refuted in the same way as perception; and analogy and scripture [are likewise refuted].

body.text: atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we say:

children.text: yadi kiñcid upalabheyaṃ pravarteyaṃ nivartayeyaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: If I were to apprehend anything, I would affirm or negate;

children.text: pratyakṣādibhir arthais tadabhāvān me 'nupālambhaḥ || 30 ||
children.translated_text: since those [pramāṇa-]objects do not exist, I am [subject to] no reproach. // NagVv 30 //

body.text: yady ahaṃ kiñcid artham upalabheyaṃ pratyakṣānumānopa + + + + hetubhiḥ pramāṇaiḥ | caturṇāṃ vā pramāṇānāṃ | anyatamānyatamena | ata evaṃ pravartayeyaṃ vārtham evāhaṃ kiñcin nopalabhate tasmān na pravartayāmi na nivartayāmi | tatraivaṃ sati yau bhavatopālambhoktaḥ | yadi pratyakṣādīnāṃ pramāṇānām anyatamena upalabhya bhāvān vinivartayasīti | nanu bhavatoktāni pramāṇāni na santi taiś ca pramāṇair api gamyārthā iti sa me bhavaty evānupālambha iti |
body.translated_text: If I were to apprehend any object through the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — perception, inference, analogy, and scripture — or through any one among the four <s>pramāṇas</s>, then indeed I would affirm or negate some object. But I do not apprehend anything whatsoever; therefore I neither affirm nor negate. This being the case, the reproach that you stated — 'If you negate entities after apprehending them through some one of the <s>pramāṇas</s> such as perception' — since indeed the <s>pramāṇas</s> you mentioned do not exist, and the objects cognized by those <s>pramāṇas</s> [also do not exist], that [reproach] is simply a non-reproach for me.
[Moreover:]

children.text: yadi ca pramāṇatas teṣāṃ teṣāṃ prasiddhir arthānām /
children.translated_text: If, moreover, the establishment of those various objects is through <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition),

children.text: teṣāṃ punaḥ prasiddhiṃ brūhi kathaṃ teṣāṃ pramāṇānāṃ || 31 ||
children.translated_text: then tell me: how is the establishment of those <s>pramāṇas</s> themselves? // NagVv 31 //

body.text: prasiddhir iti
body.translated_text: 'Establishment' means:

body.text: yadi ca pramāṇatas teṣāṃ teṣām arthānāṃ prameyānāṃ siddhiṃ manyase yathā mānair meyānāṃ | tathā teṣām idānīṃ pratyakṣānumānopamānāgamānāṃ caturṇāṃ pramāṇānāṃ kutaḥ prasiddhiḥ | yadi tāvan niḥpramāṇānāṃ pramāṇaṃ syān nādeḥ siddhis tatrāsti naiva madhyasya nāntasya | yadi punaḥ manyase pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhiḥ pramāṇato 'rthānāṃ prasiddhir iti | hīyate pratijñā |
body.translated_text: If you think that the establishment of those various objects, the <s>prameyas</s> (objects of valid cognition), is through <s>pramāṇas</s>, just as measurable things [are established] by measures — then tell me: from where is the establishment of those four <s>pramāṇas</s> — perception, inference, analogy, and scripture? If [they are established] without <s>pramāṇas</s>, there is no establishment of the beginning, nor of the middle, nor of the end. If, on the other hand, you think the establishment [of pramāṇas] is through [other] <s>pramāṇas</s> — [that] 'the establishment of objects is through <s>pramāṇas</s>' — then [your] thesis is undermined.

body.text: tathāpi
body.translated_text: Furthermore:

children.text: anyaiḥ yadi pramāṇaiḥ pramāṇasidhir bhavaty anavasthā syān /
children.translated_text: If the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> is through other <s>pramāṇas</s>, there would be an infinite regress;

children.text: nādeḥ siddhis tatrāsti naiva madhyasya nāntasya || 32 ||
children.translated_text: there is no establishment of the beginning in that [regress], nor of the middle, nor of the end. // NagVv 32 //

body.text: yadi punar manyase | pramāṇaiḥ prameyāṇāṃ prasiddhis teṣāṃ pramāṇānām anyaiḥ pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhir anavasthāprasaṅgaḥ | anavasthāprasaṅge ko doṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: If, on the other hand, you think: 'The establishment of <s>prameyas</s> is through <s>pramāṇas</s>, and the establishment of those <s>pramāṇas</s> is through other <s>pramāṇas</s>' — then there is the consequence of an infinite regress. What is the fault in the consequence of an infinite regress?

body.text: nādeḥ siddhis tatrāsti naiva madhyasya nāntasya |
body.translated_text: There is no establishment of the beginning in that [regress], nor of the middle, nor of the end.

body.text: asyānavasthāprasaṅge ādeḥ siddhir nāsti | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ teṣam api hi pramāṇānām anyaiḥ pramāṇaiḥ siddhis teṣām anyair iti nāsty ādiḥ | āder asadbhāvāt kuto madhyaṃ kuto antaḥ | tasmāt teṣāṃ pramāṇānām anyaiḥ pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhiḥ nopapadyateti |
body.translated_text: In this consequence of infinite regress, there is no establishment of the beginning. For what reason? Because the establishment of those <s>pramāṇas</s> too is through other <s>pramāṇas</s>, and those through yet others — thus there is no beginning. Since there is no beginning, from where [would there be] a middle? From where an end? Therefore, the establishment of those <s>pramāṇas</s> through other <s>pramāṇas</s> is untenable.

children.text: teṣām atha pramāṇair vinā prasiddhiḥ vihīyate vādaḥ /
children.translated_text: If, then, [there is] establishment of those [pramāṇas] without [other] <s>pramāṇas</s>, your argument is undermined;

children.text: vaiṣamikatvaṃ tasmin viśeṣahetuś ca vaktavyaḥ || 33 ||
children.translated_text: there is inequality in that, and the specific reason must be stated. // NagVv 33 //

body.text: atha manyase teṣāṃ pramāṇānāṃ vinā pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhiḥ prameyānāṃ punar arthānāṃ pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhir iti | evaṃ sati yas te vādaḥ pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhir arthānām iti hīyate vaiṣamikatvañ ca bhavati | keṣāñcit | arthānāṃ pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhiḥ keṣāñcin neti viśeṣahetuś ca vaktavyaḥ | yena hetunā keṣāṃcid arthānāṃ pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhiḥ keṣāñcin neti | sā ca nopadiṣṭaḥ tasmād iyam api kalpanā nopapanneti |
body.translated_text: If you think that the establishment of those <s>pramāṇas</s> is without [other] <s>pramāṇas</s>, while the establishment of <s>prameya</s>-objects is through <s>pramāṇas</s> — then in that case, your argument that 'the establishment of objects is through <s>pramāṇas</s>' is undermined, and there arises inequality: the establishment of some objects is through <s>pramāṇas</s> while that of some is not. And the specific reason must be stated — the reason why some objects are established through <s>pramāṇas</s> and some are not. And that [reason] has not been indicated. Therefore, this supposition too is untenable.

body.text: atrāha | pramāṇāny eva mama svātmānaṃ parātmānañ ca prasādhayanti | yathoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: [The opponent] says: My <s>pramāṇas</s> themselves establish both themselves and other things. As stated:

body.text:
dyotayati svātmānaṃ yathā hutāsaḥ tathā parātmānaṃ |
svaparātmānāv eṣāṃ prasādhayanti pramāṇāni |
body.translated_text: 'Just as fire illuminates both itself and other things, so the <s>pramāṇas</s> establish both themselves and other things —

body.text: param iva svātmānaṃ parātmānañ ceti ||
body.translated_text: their own nature as well as other things, like [they establish] other things.'

body.text: atrocyate |
body.translated_text: To this we reply:

children.text: viṣamopanyāso 'yaṃ na hy ātmānaṃ prakāśayaty agniḥ /
children.translated_text: This is an unequal comparison, for fire does not illuminate itself;

children.text: na hi tasyānupalabdhiḥ dṛṣṭā tamasīva kumbhasya || 34 ||
children.translated_text: for its non-apprehension has not been observed [anywhere], as [is the case with] a pot in darkness. // NagVv 34 //

body.text: viṣama evāyam upanyāsaḥ | agnivat pramāṇāni svātmānañ ca prasādhayanti parātmānañ ca prasādhayantīti | na hy agnir ātmānaṃ prakāśayati | yadi hi yathā prāg evāgninā aprakāśitas tamasi kumbho nopalabhyate | athottarakālam upalabhyate 'gninā prakāśitaḥ san evam eva yady agninā na prakāśitaḥ prāg agniḥ syād uttarakālam agneḥ prakāśanaṃ syāt | ataḥ svātmānaṃ prakāśayen naitad evaṃ | tasmād iyam api kalpanā nopapadyanteti |
body.translated_text: This comparison is indeed unequal — that <s>pramāṇas</s>, like fire, establish both themselves and other things. For fire does not illuminate itself. If, just as a pot that was previously not illuminated by fire is not apprehended in darkness, and then is subsequently apprehended when illuminated by fire — in the same way, if fire were previously not illuminated [by itself] and subsequently its illumination occurred, then it would illuminate itself. But this is not the case. Therefore, this supposition too is untenable.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yadi ca svātmānam ayaṃ tvadvacanena prakāśayaty agniḥ /
children.translated_text: If, according to your statement, this fire illuminates itself

children.text: param iva na tv ātmānaṃ paridhakṣyaty api hutāśaḥ || 35 ||
children.translated_text: just as [it illuminates] other things, then fire will also burn itself. // NagVv 35 //

body.text: yadi ca tvadvacanena yathā parātmānaṃ prakāśayaty agniḥ evam eva svātmānam api prakāśayaty agnir iti | nanu yathā parātmānaṃ dahati | evam eva svātmānam api dhakṣyatīti | na caitad evaṃ | tatra yad uktaṃ parātmānam iva svātmānaṃ prakāśayaty agnir iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: If, according to your statement, fire illuminates its own nature just as it illuminates other things — then surely, just as it burns other things, it would also burn itself. But this is not the case. In that regard, the statement that 'Fire illuminates itself just as it illuminates other things' — that is not [correct].

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yadi ca svaparātmānau tvadvacanena prakāśayaty agniḥ /
children.translated_text: If, according to your statement, fire illuminates both itself and other things,

children.text: prachādayiṣyati tamaḥ svaparātmānau hutāśa iva || 36 ||
children.translated_text: then darkness too, like fire, would conceal both itself and other things. // NagVv 36 //

body.text: yadi ca bhavato bhavato matena svātmāparātmānau prakāśayaty agniḥ | nanv idānīṃ pratipakṣabhūtatamo 'pi svaparātmānau chādayet | naitad iṣṭaṃ | tatra yad uktaṃ svaparātmānau prakāśayaty agnir iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: If, according to your view, fire illuminates both its own nature and other natures — then surely darkness, being the opposite, would also conceal both itself and other things. This is not accepted. In that regard, the statement that 'Fire illuminates both itself and other things' — that is not [correct].

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nāsti tamaś ca jvalane yatra ca tiṣṭhate parātmani jvalanaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no darkness in fire, nor is there darkness where fire exists, in itself or in another;

children.text: kurute kathaṃ prakāśaṃ sa hi prakāśo andhakāravadhaḥ || 37 ||
children.translated_text: how then does it produce illumination? For illumination is the destruction of darkness. || NagVv 37 ||

body.text: iha cāgnau nāsti tamaḥ | nāpi ca yatrāgnis tatrāsti tamaḥ | prakāśaś ca nāma tamasaḥ pratighātas tatra katham asya tamasaḥ | pratighātam agniḥ karoti | yasya pratighātat svaparātmānau prakāśayatīti ||
body.translated_text: Here, there is no darkness in fire. Nor is there darkness where fire is. And illumination is indeed the destruction of darkness. How then does fire destroy that darkness, by the destruction of which it illuminates itself and others?

body.text: āha | yad yasmād evaṃ nāgnau tamo 'sti | nāpi yatrāgnis tatra tamo 'sti | yasmād evaṃ svaparātmānau na prakāśayaty agniḥ | tena hy utpadyamānenaivāgninā tamasaḥ pratighataḥ kutaḥ tasmān nāgnau tamo 'sti | nāpi yatrāgniḥ tatra tamo 'sti | yasmād utpadyamāna evobhayaṃ prakāśayaty agniḥ svātmānaṃ parātmānañ ceti |
body.translated_text: The opponent says: Since it is so—there is no darkness in fire, nor is there darkness where fire is—fire destroys darkness at the very moment of arising. How? Because fire illuminates both—itself and others—at the very moment of arising.

body.text: atrocyate
body.translated_text: Here it is said:

children.text: utpadyamāna eva prakāśayaty agnir ity asadvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Fire illuminates at the very moment of arising'—this is a false assertion;

children.text: utpadyamāna eva prāpnoti tamo na hi hutāśaḥ || 38 ||
children.translated_text: for fire, at the very moment of arising, does not reach darkness. || NagVv 38 ||

body.text: ayam agnir utpadyamāna eva prakāśayati svātmānaṃ parātmānañ ceti | nāyam upapadyate vādaḥ | kasmān na hy utpadyamāna evāgniḥ tamaḥ prāpnoti | aprāptatvān naivopahanti | tamasaś cānupaghātān nāsti prakāśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This assertion—that fire illuminates itself and others at the very moment of arising—is untenable. Why? Because fire at the very moment of arising does not reach darkness. Not having reached it, it does not destroy it. And without the destruction of darkness, there is no illumination.

children.text: aprāpto 'pi jvalano yadi vā punar andhakāram upahanyāt /
children.translated_text: And if fire, even without reaching darkness, were to destroy it,

children.text: sarveṣu lokadhātuṣu tamo 'yam iha saṃsthita upahanyāt || 39 ||
children.translated_text: then, situated here, it would destroy the darkness in all world-realms. || NagVv 39 ||

body.text: athāpi manyase aprāpto 'py agnir andhakāram upahantīti | nanv idānīm iha saṃsthito agniḥ sarvalokadhātustham upahaniṣyati tamaḥ tulyāyām aprāpto na caitad evaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ | tasmād aprāpyaivāgnir andhakāram upahantīti yad iṣṭaṃ | tan na |
body.translated_text: And if you think that fire destroys darkness even without reaching it—then fire situated here would destroy the darkness in all world-realms, since the condition of not reaching is the same. But this is not observed. Therefore, the view that fire destroys darkness without reaching it is not valid.

children.text:
yadi ca svataḥ pramāṇasiddhir anapekṣya te prameyāṇi /
bhavati pramāṇasiddhiḥ nāparāpekṣā hi siddhir iti || 40 ||
children.translated_text: And if you think the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge) is by itself, independent of <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge), then the establishment of the means of knowledge would be independent—for self-establishment does not depend on another. || NagVv 40 ||

body.text: yadi cāgnivat svataḥ pramāṇasiddhir iti manyase | anapekṣāpi prameyāṇi pramāṇānāṃ siddhiḥ bhaviṣyatīti kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | na hi svataḥ param apekṣate | athāpekṣyate na svataḥ prasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: And if you think, like fire, that the establishment of the means of knowledge is by itself—then the establishment of the means of knowledge would be independent of the objects of knowledge. Why? Because what is self-established does not depend on another. And if it does depend, then it is not self-established.

body.text: atrāha | yadi nāpekṣyante prameyān arthān apramāṇāni ko doṣo bhaviṣyatīti | atrocyate |
body.translated_text: The opponent says: If the means of knowledge are not dependent on the objects of knowledge, what fault would there be? Here it is said:

children.text: anāpeksā hi prameyān arthān yadi te pramāṇasaṃsiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: If the establishment of the means of knowledge is indeed independent of the objects of knowledge,

children.text: bhavati na bhavanti kasyacid evam imāni pramāṇāni || 41 ||
children.translated_text: then these means of knowledge would not be the means of knowledge of anything. || NagVv 41 ||

body.text: yadi prameyān arthān anapekṣya siddhir bhavati pramāṇānām iti | tānīmāni pramāṇāni na kasyacit pramāṇāni bhavanti | evaṃ doṣaḥ || atha kasyacit bhavanti prāmāṇāni | naivedānīm anapekṣya prameyān arthān pramāṇāni bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: If the means of knowledge are established independently of the objects of knowledge, then those means of knowledge would not be the means of knowledge of anything. Such is the fault. But if they are means of knowledge of something, then they are not established independently of the objects of knowledge.

children.text: atha matam apekṣa siddhis teṣām iti atra bhavati ko doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, if you think there is establishment dependent on objects of knowledge, what is the fault there?

children.text: siddhasya na sādhanaṃ syān nāsiddho pekṣate hy anyat || 42 ||
children.translated_text: There would be no proof of what is already established; and what is not established does not depend on another. || NagVv 42 ||

body.text: athāpi matam apekṣya prameyān arthān pramāṇānāṃ siddhir bhavatīti | evaṃ te sati siddhasya pramāṇacatuṣṭayasya sādhanaṃ bhavatīti | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | na hy asiddhasyārthasyāpekṣaṇaṃ bhavati | na hy asiddho devadattaḥ kañcid artham apekṣate na ca siddhasya sādhanam iṣṭaṃ kṛtasya kāraṇam anupapatter iti ||
body.translated_text: And if you think the means of knowledge are established in dependence on the objects of knowledge, then in that case, what is already established—the fourfold means of knowledge—would require proof. For what reason? Because a thing not yet established does not depend on anything. Just as <s>Devadatta</s>, when not yet established, does not seek any object. And proof of what is already established is not desired, since a cause for what is already accomplished is untenable.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: sidhyanti hi prameyāṇy apekṣya yadi sarvathā pramāṇāni /
children.translated_text: If the means of knowledge are established in dependence on the objects of knowledge in every way,

children.text: bhavanti prameyasiddhir anapekṣyaiva pramāṇāni || 43 ||
children.translated_text: then the objects of knowledge are established without depending on the means of knowledge. || NagVv 43 ||

body.text: yadi prameyāṇy apekṣya pramāṇāni sidhyanti | nedānīṃ pramāṇāny apekṣya prameyāṇi sidhyanti | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ na hi sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ sādhanaṃ sādhayati | sādhanāni ca | kila prameyāṇāṃ pramāṇāni ||
body.translated_text: If the means of knowledge are established in dependence on the objects of knowledge, then the objects of knowledge are not established in dependence on the means of knowledge. Why? Because the thing to be proved does not prove the prover; and the provers are indeed the means of knowledge of the objects of knowledge.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: yadi ca prameyasiddhir anapekṣaiva bhavati pramāṇāni /
children.translated_text: And if the objects of knowledge are established without depending on the means of knowledge,

children.text: kin te pramāṇasiddhyā tāni yad arthaṃ prasiddhaṃ tata || 44 ||
children.translated_text: what use to you is the establishment of the means of knowledge? That for the sake of which they were sought is already established. || NagVv 44 ||

body.text: yadi ca manyase 'napekṣyaiva pramāṇāni prameyānāṃ prasiddhir bhavati | kim idānīṃ te pramāṇasiddhyā paryanviṣṭayā kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | yad arthaṃ hi tāni pramāṇāni paryanviṣyeran | te prameyārthā vinā pramāṇaiḥ siddhāḥ tatra kiṃ pramāṇaiḥ kṛtyaṃ |
body.translated_text: And if you think that the objects of knowledge are established without depending on the means of knowledge, then what use to you is the sought-after establishment of the means of knowledge? For what reason? The objects of knowledge for whose sake the means of knowledge would be sought are already established without the means of knowledge. Then what use are the means of knowledge?

children.text: atha tu pramāṇasiddhir bhavaty apekṣyaiva te prameyāṇi /
children.translated_text: But if the establishment of the means of knowledge is only in dependence on the objects of knowledge,

children.text: vyatyaya evaṃ sati te dhruvaṃ pramāṇaprameyāṇāṃ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: then an interchange of your means of knowledge and objects of knowledge is certain. || NagVv 45 ||

body.text: athāpi manyase 'pekṣyaiva prameyān arthāna pramāṇani bhavanti | evaṃ te sati mā bhūt pūrvoktadoṣa iti kṛtvā | evaṃ te sati vyatyayaḥ + + + + + yāṇāṃ bhavati | pramāṇāni te prameyāṇi bhavanti | prameyaiḥ sādhitatvat | pramāṇāni ca prameyāṇi bhavanti | pramāṇānāṃ sādhakatvāt |
body.translated_text: And if you think that the means of knowledge exist only in dependence on the objects of knowledge—lest the previously stated fault arise—then in that case, an interchange of the means of knowledge and objects of knowledge occurs. The means of knowledge become objects of knowledge, because they are proved by the objects. And the objects of knowledge become means of knowledge, because they are provers of the means of knowledge.

children.text: atha te pramāṇasiddhyā prameyasiddhiḥ prameyasiddhyā ca /
children.translated_text: Or if through the establishment of the means of knowledge there is establishment of the objects, and through the establishment of the objects

children.text: bhavati pramāṇasiddhiḥ nāsty ubhayasyāpi te siddhiḥ || 46 ||
children.translated_text: there is establishment of the means of knowledge—then neither of the two is established for you. || NagVv 46 ||

body.text: atha manyase pramāṇasiddhyā prameyasiddhir bhavati pramāṇāpekṣatvāt | prameyasiddhyā ca pramāṇasiddhir bhavati prameyāpekṣatvād iti || evaṃ saty ubhayasyāpi siddhir na .y. + + + + ṇaṃ
body.translated_text: And if you think: through the establishment of the means of knowledge, the establishment of the objects of knowledge occurs, because of dependence on the means; and through the establishment of the objects, the establishment of the means occurs, because of dependence on the objects—then in that case, the establishment of neither is achieved.

children.text: sidhyanti hi pramāṇair yadi prameyāṇi tāni tair evā /
children.translated_text: For if the objects of knowledge are established by the means of knowledge, those very [means]

children.text: sādhyāni ca prameyais tāni kathaṃ sādhayiṣyanti || 47 ||
children.translated_text: must be established by the objects—how then will they establish the objects? || NagVv 47 ||

body.text: yadi hi pramāṇaiḥ pramayāṇi sidhyanti tāni pramāṇāni tair eva prameyaiḥ sādhayitavyāni | nanv asiddheṣu prameyeṣu kāraṇasyāsiddhatvād asiddhāni kathaṃ sādhayisyanti prameyāṇīti |
body.translated_text: For if the objects of knowledge are established by the means of knowledge, those means of knowledge are to be established by those very objects. But since the objects are not yet established, and thus the cause is unestablished, how will the unestablished means establish the objects of knowledge?

children.text: sidhyanti ca prameyaiḥ yadi pramāṇāni tāni tair eva /
children.translated_text: And if the means of knowledge are established by the objects of knowledge, those very [objects]

children.text: sādhyāni ca prameyais tāni kathaṃ sādhayiṣyanti || 48 ||
children.translated_text: must be established by the means—how then will they establish the means? || NagVv 48 ||

body.text: yadi prameyaiḥ pramāṇāni sidhyanti tāni ca prameyāṇi tair eva pramāṇaiḥ sādhayitavyānīti | nanv asiddheṣu pramāṇeṣu kāraṇasyāsiddhatvād asiddhāni kathaṃ sādhayiṣyanti pramāṇāni |
body.translated_text: If the means of knowledge are established by the objects of knowledge, and those objects are to be established by those very means—but since the means of knowledge are not yet established, and thus the cause is unestablished, how will the unestablished objects establish the means of knowledge?

children.text: pitra yady utpādyaḥ putro yadi tena caiva putreṇa /
children.translated_text: If a son is to be produced by a father, and if by that very son

children.text: utpādyaḥ sa yadi pitā vada tatrotpādayati kaḥ kaṃ || 49 ||
children.translated_text: that father is to be produced—then tell, in that case, who produces whom? || NagVv 49 ||

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kaścit brūyāt | pitrā putra utpādanīyaḥ sa ca pitā putreṇotpādanīya iti | tatredānīṃ brūhi kena ka utpādayitavyaḥ | tathaiva khalu bhavān bravīti | pramāṇaiḥ prameyāni sādhayitavyāni tāny eva ca punaḥ pramāṇāni taiḥ prameyaiḥ tatredānīṃ tu katamaiḥ katamāni sādhayitavyāni |
