body.translated_text: Just as someone might say: 'A son is to be produced by a father, and that father is to be produced by the son.' Then tell: by whom is who to be produced? In exactly the same way, you say: 'The objects of knowledge are to be established by the means of knowledge, and those very means of knowledge by those objects.' Then in that case, which are to establish which?

children.text: kaś ca pitā kaḥ putraḥ tatra tvaṃ brūhi kathaṃ tāv ubhāv api ca /
children.translated_text: And who is the father and who is the son? Tell us how both of them

children.text: pitreputralakṣaṇadharau yato nas tatra saṃdehaḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: bear the defining characteristic of father and son—for herein lies our doubt. || NagVv 50 ||

body.text: tayoś ca pūrvopadiṣṭayoḥ pitāputrayoḥ vada kataraḥ putraḥ kataraḥ pitā ubhāv api tāv utpādakatvāt pitṛlakṣaṇadharau | utpādyatvāc ca putralakṣaṇadharāv atra naḥ sandeho bhavati | kataras tatra pitā kataras tatra putra iti | evam eva yāny etāni bhavati | pramāṇaprameyaṇi | tatra katarāṇi pramāṇāni katarāṇi prameyāṇi | ubhayāny api hy etāni pramāṇāni tāni prameyāṇi sādhyatvāt prameyāṇīti | atra naḥ sandeho bhavati | katarāṇy atra pramāṇāni katarāṇi prameyāṇīti |
body.translated_text: And regarding those two—the father and son described above—tell which is the son and which is the father. Both of them, because of being producers, bear the defining characteristic of a father; and because of being produced, they bear the defining characteristic of a son. Herein lies our doubt: which is the father and which the son? In exactly the same way, regarding those means of knowledge and objects of knowledge—which are the means and which are the objects? Both of these are means of knowledge, and because of being proved, they are objects of knowledge. Herein lies our doubt: which here are the means of knowledge and which are the objects of knowledge?

children.text: naiva svataḥ prasiddhir na parasparataḥ pramāṇair vā /
children.translated_text: The means of knowledge are established neither by themselves, nor by each other, nor by other means of knowledge,

children.text: bhavati na ca prameyaiḥ na cāpy akasmāt pramāṇānāṃ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: nor by the objects of knowledge, nor without any reason at all. || NagVv 51 ||

body.text: na svataḥ prasiddhiḥ pratyakṣasya tenaiva pratyakṣeṇānumānasya tenaivānumāne | upamānasya tenaivopamānena | āgamasya tenaivāgamena || nāpi parasyāt pratyakṣasyānumānopamānāgamair anumānasya pratyakṣopamānāgamair upamānasya pratyakṣānumānāgamaiḥ | āgamasya pratyakṣānumānopamānaiḥ | nāpi pratyakṣānumānopamānāgamād anyaiḥ pratyakṣānumānopamānāgamair yathāsvaṃ nāpi prameyaiḥ samastavyastaiḥ svaviṣayaparaviṣatāgṛhītaiḥ nāpy akasmān nāsti samuccayena | eteṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ pūrvoddiṣṭānāṃ viṃśas triṃśac catvāriśat ṣaṭviṃśatir vā tatra yad uktaṃ | pramāṇādhigamyatvāt prameyāṇāṃ bhāvānāṃ santi tu prameyā bhāvās tāni ca pramāṇāni yais tu pramāṇaiḥ prameyā bhāvāḥ santaś ca bhāvāḥ samādhigatā iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: There is no self-establishment of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) by that very <s>pratyakṣa</s>, nor of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) by that very <s>anumāna</s>, nor of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) by that very <s>upamāna</s>, nor of <s>āgama</s> (testimony) by that very <s>āgama</s>. Nor is there establishment by another: <s>pratyakṣa</s> is not established by <s>anumāna</s>, <s>upamāna</s>, and <s>āgama</s>; <s>anumāna</s> is not established by <s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>upamāna</s>, and <s>āgama</s>; <s>upamāna</s> is not established by <s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>anumāna</s>, and <s>āgama</s>; <s>āgama</s> is not established by <s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>anumāna</s>, and <s>upamāna</s>. Nor by other <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) distinct from <s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>anumāna</s>, <s>upamāna</s>, and <s>āgama</s> respectively; nor by <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) collectively or individually, whose own and others' domains are not apprehended; nor without any cause; nor by combination. These reasons enumerated earlier number twenty, thirty, forty, or twenty-six. Therefore, what was stated — that because <s>prameyas</s> (knowable entities) are apprehended through <s>pramāṇas</s>, these <s>prameyas</s> exist, and those <s>pramāṇas</s> by which the <s>prameyas</s> are known also exist, and the entities are thus established — that is not so.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktam |
body.translated_text: And as for what you have stated:

body.text: kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmāvasthāvidaś ca manyante |

children.text: kuśalaṃ janasvabhāvaṃ manyante śeṣeṣv apy eṣa viniyogaḥ | [7]
children.translated_text: the wholesome nature (<s>kuśala-svabhāva</s>) of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; and this same application holds for the rest. [7]

body.translated_text: Those who know the classification of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) consider

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we reply:

children.text: kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmāvasthavido brūvate yat /
children.translated_text: As for what those who know the classification of <s>dharmas</s> say about wholesome <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: kuśalasvabhāvam evaṃ pravibhāgenābhidheyaḥ syāt || 52 ||
children.translated_text: that wholesome intrinsic nature (<s>kuśala-svabhāva</s>) should be specified by you through detailed classification. // <s>NagVv</s>_52 //

body.text: kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmāvasthavidaḥ kuśalaṃ janasvabhāvaṃ manyante | sa ca bhavatā pravibhāgenopadeṣṭavyaḥ | syād ayaṃ sa kuśalaḥ svabhāvaḥ ime te kuśalā dharmā iti | idaṃ tatkuśalavijñānam ayaṃ kuśalavijñānasvabhāva evaṃ sarveṣāṃ na caitad evaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ | tasmād yad uktam upadiṣṭaḥ svabhāvo dharmāṇām iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: Those who know the classification of <s>dharmas</s> consider the wholesome nature to be the intrinsic nature of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And that should be taught by you through detailed classification: 'This is that wholesome intrinsic nature; these are the wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; this is the consciousness of the wholesome; this is the intrinsic nature of wholesome consciousness' — and so on for all. But this has not been shown to be so. Therefore, what was stated — that the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> has been taught — that is not so.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yadi ca pratītya kuśalaḥ svabhāva utpadyate sa kuśalānām /
children.translated_text: If the wholesome intrinsic nature arises dependently,

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ parabhāvaḥ svabhāva eva kathaṃ bhavati || 53 ||
children.translated_text: how can that which is of other-nature (<s>parabhāva</s>) be the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>? // <s>NagVv</s>_53 //

body.text: yadi ca kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvo hetupratyayasāmagrīṃ pratītyotpadyate | parabhāvād utpannaḥ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kathaṃ svabhāvo bhavati | evam evākuśalaprabhṛtīnāṃ | tatra yad uktaṃ | kuśalāvyākṛtānāṃ nā .y. + + + dharmāṇāṃ kuśalaḥ svabhāvopadiṣṭaḥ | evam akuśalānām akuśalādir iti | tan na ||
body.translated_text: If the intrinsic nature of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> arises dependent upon the assemblage of causes and conditions, then how can what has arisen from other-nature be the intrinsic nature of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>? The same applies to unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and so forth. Therefore, what was stated — that the wholesome intrinsic nature of wholesome and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s> has been taught, and likewise the unwholesome nature of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and so on — that is not so.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: atha na pratītya kiñcit svabhāva utpadyate sa kuśalānām /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, intrinsic nature arises without depending on anything,

children.text: dharmāṇām evaṃ syād vāso na brahmacaryasya || 54 ||
children.translated_text: then for wholesome <s>dharmas</s> there would be no dwelling in the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). // <s>NagVv</s>_54 //

body.text: atha manyase | na kiñcit pratītya kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kuśalasvabhāva utpadyate | evam akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām akuśalaḥ avyākṛtānām avyākṛta iti | evaṃ saty abrahmacaryavāso bhavati kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | pratītyasamutpādasya hi evaṃ sati pratyākhyānaṃ bhavati | pratītyasamutpādasya pratyākhyānāt pratītyasamutpādadarśaṇaṃ pratyākhyānaṃ bhavati | na hy avidyamānasya pratītyasamutpādasya darśanam utpadyamānaṃ bhavati | asati pratītyasamutpādadarśane dharmadarśanaṃ na bhavati | uktaṃ hi | bhagavatā yo hi bhikṣavaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati sa dharmaṃ paśyati | dharmadarśanābhāvād brahmacaryavāsābhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: If you think that the wholesome intrinsic nature of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> arises without depending on anything — and likewise the unwholesome nature of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and the indeterminate nature of indeterminate <s>dharmas</s> — then in that case there would be no dwelling in the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). Why? Because in that case there would be a rejection of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). From the rejection of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, the seeing of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> would be rejected. For the seeing of a non-existent <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> cannot arise. In the absence of seeing <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, the seeing of <s>Dharma</s> does not occur. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'O monks, whoever sees <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> sees the <s>Dharma</s>.' From the absence of <s>Dharma</s>-seeing, there is absence of dwelling in the holy life.

body.text: athavā pratītyasamutpādapratyākhyānāt | duḥkhasamudāyapratyākhyānaṃ bhavati | pratītyasamutpādo hi duḥkhasya samudayaḥ | duḥkhasamudayasya pratyākhyānād duḥkhapratyākhyānaṃ bhavati | asati hi samudaye tat kuto duḥkhaṃ samudeṣyati | duḥkhasamudayapratyākhyānāc ca duḥkhanirodhasya pratyākhyānaṃ | asati hi duḥkhasamudaye kasya prahāṇān nirodho bhaviṣyati | asati hi duḥkhanirodhe kasya prāptaye mārgo bhaviṣyati | duḥkhanirodhagāmī | evaṃ caturṇām āryasatyānām abhāvāc chrāmaṇyaphalābhāvaḥ | satyadarśanādiśramaṇyaphalāni samādhigamyante | śrāmaṇyaphalānām abhāvād abrahmacaryavāsa iti ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, from the rejection of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, there would be a rejection of the origination of suffering. For <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is the origination of suffering. From the rejection of the origination of suffering, there would be a rejection of suffering itself. For in the absence of origination, from where would suffering arise? And from the rejection of the origination of suffering, there would be a rejection of the cessation of suffering. For in the absence of the origination of suffering, through the abandonment of what would cessation occur? In the absence of the cessation of suffering, for the attainment of what would there be a path — a path leading to the cessation of suffering? Thus, from the non-existence of the four <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths), there would be no fruits of the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇyaphala</s>). For the fruits of the ascetic life are attained through seeing the truths and so forth. From the non-existence of the fruits of the ascetic life, there would be no dwelling in the holy life.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nādharmo dharmo vā satyavyavahārāś ca lokikā ni syuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness) and <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) would not exist, nor would conventional worldly transactions,

children.text: nityāś ca sarvabhāvāḥ syuḥ nityatvād ahetumataḥ || 55 ||
children.translated_text: and all entities would be eternal; being eternal, they would be without cause. // <s>NagVv</s>_55 //

body.text: evaṃ sati pratītyasamutpādaṃ pratyācakṣaṇasya bhavataḥ ko doṣa prasajyate | dharmo na bhavati adharmo na bhavati | saṃvyavahārāś ca laukikā na sambhavanti | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ pratītyasamutpannaṃ hy etat sarvam asati pratītyasamutpāde kuto bhaviṣyati | api ca sasvabhāvo 'pratītyasamutpanno nirhetuko nityaḥ syāt | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ nirhetukā hi bhāvā nityās tatra sa eva cābrahmacaryavāsaḥ prasajyet svasiddhāntavirodhaś ca | kiṃ kāraṇam anityā hi bhagavatā sarve saṃskārā nirdeṣṭās te svabhāvanityatvān nityā hi bhavanti |
body.translated_text: In that case, what fault befalls you who reject <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>? There would be no <s>dharma</s>, no <s>adharma</s>, and worldly conventional transactions would not be possible. Why? Because all this is dependently originated; in the absence of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, how could it exist? Furthermore, what possesses intrinsic nature and is not dependently originated would be causeless and therefore eternal. Why? Because entities without causes are eternal. And in that case, the same consequence of no dwelling in the holy life would follow, along with contradiction of one's own doctrine. Why? Because all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) have been declared impermanent by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, yet due to the eternality of their intrinsic nature, they would be permanent.

children.text: eṣa cākuśaleṣv avyākṛteṣu nairyāṇādiṣu ca doṣas /
children.translated_text: And this same fault applies to unwholesome, indeterminate, and <s>nairyāṇika</s> (conducive to liberation) <s>dharmas</s> and so forth;

children.text: tasmāt sarvaṃ saṃskṛtam asaṃskṛtaṃ te bhavaty evaṃ || 56 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, all that is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) becomes for you unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). // <s>NagVv</s>_56 //

body.text: yaś caiṣa kuśaleṣu nirdeṣṭaḥ kalpaḥ sa evākuśaleṣu sa evāvyākṛteṣu sa evānairyāṇikaprabhṛtiṣu doṣas tasmāt sarvam idaṃ saṃskṛtam asaṃskṛtaṃ saṃpadyate || kiṃkāraṇaṃ heto hy asaty utpādasthitibhaṅgā na bhavanti | utpādasthitibhaṅgeṣv asatsu saṃskṛtalakṣaṇābhāvāt | sarvaṃ saṃskṛtam asaṃskṛtaṃ saṃpadyate | tatra yad uktaṃ kuśalādīnāṃ bhāvānāṃ svabhāvasadbhāvād aśūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: And this same analysis that was set forth regarding wholesome <s>dharmas</s> applies equally to unwholesome, to indeterminate, and to those beginning with the non-conducive-to-liberation and so forth. Therefore, all that is conditioned becomes unconditioned. Why? Because in the absence of causes, arising, persistence, and destruction do not occur. In the absence of arising, persistence, and destruction, due to the absence of the marks of the conditioned, all that is conditioned becomes unconditioned. Therefore, what was stated — that because the intrinsic nature of wholesome and other entities truly exists, all entities are non-empty — that is not so.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: And as for what you have stated:

body.text: yadi ca na bhavet svabhāvo bhāvānāṃ na svabhāva ity evaṃ

children.text: nāmāpi bhaved evaṃ nāma hi nirvastukaṃ nāsti | [9]
children.translated_text: would not exist, for a name without a referent does not exist. [9]

body.translated_text: If there were no intrinsic nature of entities, then even the name 'without intrinsic nature'

children.text: yaḥ sadbhūtaṃ nāma brūyāt sasvabhāva ity evam /
children.translated_text: Whoever would say that a name is real and possesses intrinsic nature,

children.text: bhavatā prativaktavyo nāma brūmaś ca na vayaṃ sata || 57 ||
children.translated_text: that person should be refuted by you; but we do not say that the name is real. // <s>NagVv</s>_57 //

body.text: yo nāma sadbhūtaṃ brūyāt sasvabhāva iti sa bhavatā prativaktavyaḥ syāt | yasya sadbhūtaṃ nāma svabhāvasya | tasmāt tenāpi svabhāvena sadbhūtena bhavitavyaṃ | na hy asadbhūtasya svabhāvasya sadbhūtaṃ nāma bhavatīti | na punar vayaṃ nāma sadbhūtaṃ brūmas tad api hi svabhāvasyābhāvān nāma niḥsvabhāvatvāt śūnyaṃ śūnyatvād asadbhūtam | tatra yad bhavatoktaṃ nāmasadbhāvāt sadbhūtaḥ svahhāvā iti | tan na ||
body.translated_text: Whoever would say that a name is real and possesses intrinsic nature — that person should be refuted by you, for that name would belong to an intrinsic nature that is real, and therefore that intrinsic nature too would have to be real. For a real name does not belong to an unreal intrinsic nature. But we do not say that a name is real, for due to the absence of intrinsic nature, the name too, being devoid of intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>), is empty (<s>śūnya</s>), and being empty, is unreal. Therefore, what you have stated — that because the name exists, intrinsic nature is real — that is not so.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nāmāsad iti ca yad idaṃ tat kiṃ nu sato bhavaty utāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: And this claim that the name is unreal — does that apply to what exists or to what does not exist?

children.text: yadi hi sato yady asato dvidhāpi te hīyate vādaḥ || 58 ||
children.translated_text: Whether it applies to what exists or to what does not exist, in either case your position is defeated. // <s>NagVv</s>_58 //

body.text: yac caitan nāmāsad iti tat kiṃ sataḥ asataḥ | yadi hi satas tan nāma yady asata ubhayathāpi pratijñā hīyate | tatra yadi tāvat sata | asad iti pratijñā hīyate | na hīdanīṃ tad asad idānīṃ sat* athāsata | asad iti nāma yā pratijñā asadbhūtasya nāma na bhavati astitvasvabhāva iti nāma tasmāt sadbhūtaḥ svabhāva iti | sā hīnā ||
body.translated_text: And as for this objection that 'the name is unreal' — does it apply to what exists or to what does not exist? If to what exists, then the claim that it is unreal is defeated, for what is now existent cannot now be non-existent. If to what does not exist — the claim 'it is unreal,' meaning that a name does not belong to what is unreal, and the assertion that intrinsic nature is therefore real because of its nature of existence — that too is defeated.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ śūnyatvañ copapāditaṃ pūrvam /
children.translated_text: The emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) of all entities has been previously established by us;

children.text: sa upālambhaḥ tasmād bhavaty ayañ cāpratijñāyāḥ || 59 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, this objection also applies to what is not our thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>). // <s>NagVv</s>_59 //

body.text: iha cāsmābhiḥ pūrvam eva sarveṣāṃ bhāvānaṃ vistarataḥ śūnyatvam upapāditam | tatra prāg nāmano 'pi śūnyatvam uktaṃ saṃbhavā aśūnyatvaṃ parigṛhya pravṛtto vaktuṃ | yadi bhāvānāṃ svābhāvo na syād asvabhāva iti nāmāpīdan na syād iti | tasmād apratijñopālambho yaṃ bhavataḥ saṃpadyate | na hi vayaṃ nāma sadbhūtam iti brūmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, we have previously established in detail the emptiness of all entities. There, the emptiness of the name too was stated earlier. Yet the opponent, having assumed non-emptiness, has proceeded to argue: 'If there were no intrinsic nature of entities, then even the name "without intrinsic nature" would not exist.' Therefore, this objection of yours amounts to a criticism of what is not our thesis. For we do not say that the name is real.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: And as for what you have stated:

body.text: atha vidyate svabhāvas sa ca dharmāṇāṃ na vidyate sa tasmāt

children.text: dharmair vinā svabhāvaḥ sa yasya tad yuktam upadeṣṭuṃ | [10]
children.translated_text: it would be proper to teach an intrinsic nature that exists apart from <s>dharmas</s>. [10]

body.translated_text: If intrinsic nature exists but does not belong to <s>dharmas</s>, then

children.text: atha vidyate svabhāvaḥ sa ca dharmāṇāṃ na vidyatat iti idam /
children.translated_text: As for the apprehension that 'if intrinsic nature exists but does not belong to <s>dharmas</s>,'

children.text: āśaṅkitaṃ yad uktaṃ bhavaty anāśaṅkitaṃ tac ca || 60 ||
children.translated_text: what has been stated as an objection is in fact no objection at all. // <s>NagVv</s>_60 //

body.text: na hi vayaṃ dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaṃ pratiṣedhayāmaḥ | dharmavinirmuktasya vā kasyacid arthasya svabhāvam abhyupagacchāmaḥ | nanv evaṃ sati ya upālambho bhavati | yadi dharmā niḥsvabhāvāḥ kasya khalv idānīm anyasyārthasya dharmavinirmuktasya svabhāvo bhavati | sa yuktam evopadeṣṭam iti | dūrāpakṛṣṭam evaitat bhavati |
body.translated_text: For we do not negate the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of <s>dharmas</s> (entities), nor do we accept the <s>svabhāva</s> of some object apart from <s>dharmas</s>. If this is so, then the objection that arises — "If <s>dharmas</s> are without <s>svabhāva</s>, then of what other entity, apart from <s>dharmas</s>, would there be <s>svabhāva</s>?" — that has been properly answered. This objection is entirely far-fetched.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now, as to what you have said:

body.text: sata eva pratiṣedho nāsti ghaṭo geha ity ayaṃ yasmāt |

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ pratiṣedho 'yaṃ mataḥ svabhāvasya te tasmāt | [11] ity
children.translated_text: this negation is observed; therefore your negation is of <s>svabhāva</s> [that exists]." [11]

body.translated_text: "Negation applies only to what exists — as in 'there is no pot in the house' —

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we reply:

children.text: sata eva pratiṣedho yadi śūnyatvaṃ nanv apratisiddham idam /
children.translated_text: If negation applies only to what exists, then is <s>śūnyatva</s> (emptiness) not unrefuted?

children.text: pratiṣedhayate hi hhavān bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ || 61 ||
children.translated_text: For you negate the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> in entities. // <s>NagVv</s> 61 //

body.text: yadi svata eva pratiṣedho bhavati | nāmato bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ pratiṣedhayati | nanu pratisidhaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ tvadvacanena | pratiṣedhayasi tvaṃ sadbhāvāt | niḥsvabhāvatvasya ca sarvabhāvānāṃ pratisidhatvāt | pratisiddhā śūnyateti
body.translated_text: If negation exists intrinsically, then by your very statement you negate the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> in all entities. Is not the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> in all entities then established by your own words? You negate because [negation] exists. And since the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> in all entities is established, emptiness is established.

children.text: pratiṣedhayase atha tvaṃ śūnyatvaṃ tac ca nāsti śūnyatvam /
children.translated_text: But if you negate <s>śūnyatva</s> (emptiness), and that <s>śūnyatva</s> does not exist,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ sata iti te nanv eṣa vihīyate vādaḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: then your thesis that "negation applies only to what exists" is thereby abandoned. // <s>NagVv</s> 62 //

body.text: atha śūnyatvaṃ pratiṣedhayasi tvaṃ | sarvabhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ śūnyatvaṃ nāsti tac ca śūnyatvam | yā tarhi te pratijñā sataḥ pratiṣedho bhavati nāsata iti sā hīnā ||
body.translated_text: But if you negate <s>śūnyatva</s> — the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> in all entities — and that <s>śūnyatva</s> does not exist, then your thesis that "negation applies to what exists, not to what does not exist" is undermined.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: pratiṣedhayāmi nāhaṃ kiñcit pratiṣedhyam asti na ca kiñcit /
children.translated_text: I do not negate anything, nor is there anything to be negated.

children.text: tasmāt pratiṣedhayasīty adhilaya eva tvayā kriyate || 63 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in saying "you negate," you commit a distortion. // <s>NagVv</s> 63 //

body.text: evam api tu kṛtvā yady ahaṃ kiñcit pratiṣedhayāmi tato yuktam eva vaktuṃ syāt | na caivahaṃ kiñcit pratiṣedhayāmi tasmān na kiñcit

children.text: prati
children.translated_text: to be

children.text: ṣedhavyam asti | tasmāt śūnyeṣu sarvabhāveṣv avidyamāne pratiṣedhye pratiṣedhayasīty eṣa tvayātra sadbhūto 'dhilayaḥ kriyata iti ||
children.translated_text: negated. Therefore, when all entities are empty and there is nothing to be negated, in saying "you negate" you commit a real distortion here.

body.translated_text: Even granting this: if I were negating something, then it would indeed be proper to speak thus. But I do not negate anything whatsoever; therefore there is nothing

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now, as to what you have said:

body.text: atha nāsti sa svabhāvaḥ kin nu pratiṣidhyate tvayānena

children.text: vacanena rte vacanāt pratiṣedhaḥ sidhyate hy asataḥ || [12]
children.translated_text: statement? For negation of what does not exist is established even without a statement." [12]

body.translated_text: "If that <s>svabhāva</s> does not exist, what then is negated by you with this

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we reply:

children.text: yac cāhaṃ te vacanād asataḥ pratiṣedhavacanasiddhir iti /
children.translated_text: As for your claim that negation of what does not exist is established by mere statement,

children.text: atra jñāpayate vāg asad iti tan na pratinihanti || 64 ||
children.translated_text: here speech makes known that something does not exist; it does not destroy it. // <s>NagVv</s> 64 //

body.text: ya ca bhavān bravīti | sate 'pi vacanād asataḥ pratiṣedhaḥ pratisiddhaḥ tatra kin niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ iti | etad vacanaṃ karotīti || atra brūmaḥ niḥsvabhāvā iti etat khalu vacanaṃ na niḥsvabhāvān sarvabhāvān karoti | kintv asata svabhāva bhāvānām asata svabhāvānām iti jñāpayati | tatra kaścit brūyād avidyamāhagṛhe devadattas tam asti gṛhe devadatta iti | tatrainaṃ kaścit pratibrūyān nāstīti | na tad. + + + + + devadattasyāsaṃbhavāṃ karoti | kintu jñāpayati kevalam asadbhāvaṃ gṛhe devadattasyeti || tadvā nāsti svabhāvo bhāvānām ity etadvacanaṃ na svabhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ karoti | bhāveṣu svabhāvasyābhāvaṃ jñāpayati || tatra yad bhavatoktaṃ kim asati svabhāve nāsti svabhāva ity etadvacanaṃ karoti | ṛte 'pi vacanāt prasiddhiḥ svabhāvasyābhāva iti | tat te na yuktaṃ
body.translated_text: And you say: "Even in the case of what exists, the negation of what does not exist is accomplished by statement; what then does the statement 'all entities are without <s>svabhāva</s>' accomplish?" To this we reply: the statement 'without <s>svabhāva</s>' does not make all entities devoid of <s>svabhāva</s>. Rather, it makes known that the <s>svabhāva</s> of entities does not exist. Suppose someone says "<s>Devadatta</s> is in the house" when <s>Devadatta</s> is not present in the house. Someone else replies "He is not there." That [...] does not cause <s>Devadatta</s>'s non-existence; it merely makes known the absence of <s>Devadatta</s> in the house. Likewise, the statement 'entities have no <s>svabhāva</s>' does not make <s>svabhāva</s> become devoid of <s>svabhāva</s>; it makes known the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> in entities. As to what you have said — "Does the statement 'there is no <s>svabhāva</s>' accomplish this when <s>svabhāva</s> does not exist? Even without a statement, the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> is established" — that is not valid for you.

body.text: yad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: As was said:

body.text: bālānām iva mṛgatṛṣṇāyāṃ sa yathājalagrāhaḥ |

children.text: evaṃ mithyāgrāhaḥ syāt te prasidhyate hy asataḥ | [13]
children.translated_text: so would your false apprehension be; for [you claim] what does not exist is established." [13]

body.translated_text: "Just as children might grasp at water in a mirage,

body.text: yat punar bhavato mṛgātṛṣṇāyām ity atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, as to your mirage example, here we reply:

children.text: mṛgatṛṣṇādṛṣṭānte yaḥ punar uktaṃ tvayā mahāṃś carcaḥ /
children.translated_text: Regarding the great objection you have raised concerning the mirage analogy,

children.text: tatrāpi nirṇayaṃ śṛṇu yathā sa dṛṣṭānta upapannaḥ || 65 ||
children.translated_text: hear also the resolution there — how that example is fitting. // <s>NagVv</s> 65 //

body.text: ya eva tvayā mṛgatṛṣṇādṛṣṭānte mahāṃś carca uktaḥ | tatrāpi tayā nirṇayaḥ sa śrūyatāṃ upapanna eva dṛṣṭānto bhavati |
body.translated_text: The very great objection you have raised concerning the mirage analogy — hear the resolution regarding that too: the example is indeed fitting.

children.text: sa yadi svabhāvataḥ syād bhāvo na syāt pratītya samudbhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: If that apprehension existed by <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), it would not have arisen dependently.

children.text: yaś ca pratītya hhavati grāho nanu śūnyatā saiva || 66 ||
children.translated_text: And that which arises dependently — is that not <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) itself? // <s>NagVv</s> 66 //

body.text: yadi ca mṛgatṛṣṇāyāṃ sa yathājalagrāhaḥ svabhāvataḥ syāt | na syāt pratītyasamutpanno | yato mṛgatṛṣṇāñ ca pratītya viparītañ ca darśanaṃ pratītya yoniśomanaskārañ ca pratītya prādurbhūto ataḥ pratītyasamutpannaḥ yataś ca pratītyasamutpanno 'taḥ svabhāvataḥ śūnya eva | yathā pūrvam uktaṃ tathā
body.translated_text: If the apprehension of water in a mirage existed by <s>svabhāva</s>, it would not be dependently arisen. Since it arises dependent on the mirage, dependent on distorted perception, and dependent on improper mental attention — therefore it is dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>). And since it is dependently arisen, it is empty of <s>svabhāva</s>. As was stated before, so it is.

body.text: kiñcānyat |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yadi ca svabhāvataḥ syād grāhaḥ kas taṃ vinivartayed grāham /
children.translated_text: If the apprehension existed by <s>svabhāva</s>, who could turn back that apprehension?

children.text: śeṣeṣv apy eṣa vidhiḥ tasmād eṣo 'nupālambhaḥ || 67 ||
children.translated_text: The same method applies to all remaining [entities]; therefore this is non-apprehension [of intrinsic nature]. // <s>NagVv</s> 67 //

body.text: yadi ca mṛgatṛṣṇāyāṃ jalagrāhaḥ svabhāvataḥ syāt | ka eva taṃ vinivartayetā | na hi svabhāvaḥ śakyo nivartayituṃ | tathāgner uṣṇatvam apāṃ dravatvam ākāśasya niravavaraṇatvaṃ | dṛṣṭaṃ cāsya vinivartanaṃ | tasmāc chūnyasvabhāvaḥ grāhaḥ | yadā caitad evaṃ śeṣeṣv api dharmeṣv eṣa kramaḥ pratyavagantavyaḥ grāhyapravṛttiṣu pañcasu | tatra yad bhavato + + + + pād aśūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti tan na ||
body.translated_text: If the apprehension of water in a mirage existed by <s>svabhāva</s>, who indeed could turn it back? For <s>svabhāva</s> cannot be turned back — just as the heat of fire, the fluidity of water, and the unobstructedness of space [cannot be removed]. Yet its cessation is observed. Therefore the apprehension is empty of <s>svabhāva</s>. And when this is so, the same procedure should be understood with respect to all remaining <s>dharmas</s> as well, in the five modes of apprehension of objects. As to what you have said [...] that all entities are non-empty — that is not so.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now, as to what you have said:

body.text:
hetoś ca te na siddhir naiḥsvabbāvyāt kuto hi te hetuḥ
nirhetukasya siddhir na copapannāsya te 'rthasya [l7] iti ||
body.translated_text: "Your reason (<s>hetu</s>) is not established either, for due to absence of <s>svabhāva</s>, how can you have a reason? And the establishment of your thesis without a reason is not tenable." [17]

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we reply:

children.text: etena hetvabhāvaḥ pratyuktaḥ pūrvam eva sa samatvāt /
children.translated_text: By this, the absence of a reason has already been answered previously, since the case is the same —

children.text: mṛgatṛṣṇādṛṣṭāntavyāvṛttividhau ya uktaḥ prāg || 68 ||
children.translated_text: by the method of refuting [the objection] through the mirage analogy stated before. // <s>NagVv</s> 68 //

body.text: etenaiva cedānīṃ carcena pūrvoktena hetvabhāvo 'pi pratyavagantavyaḥ | ya eva hi carcaḥ pūrvasmin hetāv uktaḥ ṣaṭkapratiṣe + + + + + + hāpi carcayitavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this very discussion stated previously, the absence of a reason should also be understood. For the very same objection that was raised regarding the previous reason, the sixfold refutation [...] should also be applied here.

body.text: yat punar bhavatoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now, as to what you have said:

children.text: pūrvaṃ cet pratiṣedhaḥ paścāt pratiṣedhyam ily anupapannaṃ |
children.translated_text: "If the negation comes before and the thing negated after, that is untenable;

children.text: paścāc cānupapanno yugapac ca yataḥ svabhāvo 'sana || [20]
children.translated_text: and [if it comes] after, that too is untenable; and simultaneously — because <s>svabhāva</s> does not exist [in any of the three times]." [20]

body.text: atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this we reply:

children.text: yat traikālye hetuḥ pratyuktaṃ pūrvam eva sa samatvāt /
children.translated_text: The argument concerning the three times has already been answered previously, since the case is the same.

children.text: traikālyapratihetuś ca śūnyabhāvādinā prāptaḥ || 69 ||
children.translated_text: And the counter-argument regarding the three times is arrived at through [the principle of] empty nature, etc. // <s>NagVv</s> 69 //

body.text: sa eṣa hetuḥ traikālye pratiṣedhavācī sa tūktottaraḥ pratyavamantaḥ | kasmāt sādhyasamatvāt | yathā hi pratiṣedhas traikālye nopapady.e + + + + + + pratiṣedhapratiṣedhe 'pi | tasmāt pratiṣedhapratiṣedhye 'sati bhavān manyate pratiṣedhaḥ pratisiddha iti tan na | yataś caiṣa trikālapratiṣedhavācī hetur eṣa eva śūnyatāvādināṃ prāptaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvapratiṣedhakatvān na bhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: This very argument asserting [the impossibility of] negation in the three times has already been answered. Why? Because it is equal to what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>). For just as negation is not tenable in the three times, [...] so too in the negation of [that] negation. Therefore, since the negation of negation does not hold, you think "negation is refuted" — but that is not so. And this argument asserting [the impossibility of] negation in the three times is arrived at by the proponents of <s>śūnyatā</s>, since it negates the <s>svabhāva</s> of all entities — it does not [serve] you.

body.text: atha vā katham etad uktottaraṃ |
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, how has this been answered?

body.text:
pratiṣedhayāmi nāhaṃ kiñcit pratiṣedhyam asti na ca kiñcit
tasmāt pratiṣedhayasīty adhilaya eṣa tvayā kriyata [63] iti ||
body.translated_text: "I do not negate anything, nor is there anything to be negated; therefore, in saying 'you negate,' you commit a distortion." [63]

body.text: atha manyase triṣv api kāleṣu + + + + + + + dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvakālīno 'pi hetuḥ uttarakālīno 'pi | yugapatkālīno 'pi hetuḥ | kathaṃ pūrvakalīnaḥ | yathā pitā putrasya tvadvacanena paścātkālīnaḥ | yathā śiṣyācāryasya yugapatkālīnaḥ yathā pradīpaḥ prakāśasyeti || atra brūmaḥ | na caitad eva yuktā hy etasmiṃ traye pūrvadoṣaḥ || api ca punaḥ yady evaṃ kamaḥ | pratiṣedhasadbhāvas tvayābhyupagamyate | pratijñāhāniś ca te bhavati | e + + + + + + + svabhā + + + .edho 'pi si + + bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: Now, if you think that in all three times [...] a reason is observed — whether prior in time, subsequent in time, or simultaneous in time — how is it prior in time? As a father is to a son. [How is it] subsequent in time, by your account? As a student is to a teacher. [How is it] simultaneous? As a lamp is to its light. To this we reply: none of these are valid, for in all three cases the previous flaw applies. Moreover, if the order is thus, and you accept the existence of negation, then your thesis is lost. [...] The negation too would be established [as existing by <s>svabhāva</s>].

children.text: prabhavati ca śūnyateyaṃ yasya prabhavanti tasya sarvārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: For whom <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is tenable, for him all things are tenable.

children.text: prabhavati na tasya kinna prabhavati śūnyatā yasyeti || 70 ||
children.translated_text: For whom <s>śūnyatā</s> is not tenable, for him nothing is tenable. // <s>NagVv</s> 70 //

body.text: yasya śūnyateyaṃ prabhavati tasya sarvārthā laukikalokottarāḥ prabhavanti | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | yasya hi śūnyatā prabhavati tasya pratītyasamutpādaḥ prabhavati | yasya pratītyasamutpādaḥ prabhavati tasya catvāry āryasatyāni prabhavanti | yasya catvāry āryasatyāni + + + + + + + maṇyaphalāni bhavanti | sarvaviśeṣādhigamaḥ bhavanti | yasya sarvaviśeṣādhigamāḥ prabhavanti | tasya trīṇi raṃāṇi buddhadharmasaṃghāḥ prabhavanti | yasya pratītyasamutpādaḥ prabhavanti tasya dharmo dharmahetur dharmaphalañ ca prabhavanti | tasyādharmo 'dharmahetuś cādharmaphalañ ca prabhavati | tasya kleśaḥ kleśasamudayaḥ kleśavastūni ca prabhavanti | yasyaitat sarvaṃ bhavati pūrvoktaṃ tasya sugatiṃ durgatiṃ vyavasthā + + + + + + + gatidurgatigamanaṃ | sugatidurgatigāmī mārgaḥ | sugatidurgatigamanavyatikramaṇaṃ sugatidurgativyatikramopāyaḥ sarvasaṃvyavahārāś ca lokikāḥ svayam adhigantavyāḥ | anayā diśā kiñcit śakyaṃ vacanopadeṣṭam iti |
body.translated_text: For whom this <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is tenable, for him all purposes — both worldly and supramundane — are tenable. What is the reason? For whom <s>śūnyatā</s> is tenable, for him <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) is tenable. For whom <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is tenable, for him the four <s>Āryasatyas</s> (Noble Truths) are tenable. For whom the four Noble Truths [are tenable], ... the fruits of the ascetic life are [tenable]. All special attainments are [tenable]. For whom all special attainments are tenable, for him the three jewels — Buddha, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> — are tenable. For whom <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is tenable, for him <s>dharma</s> (virtue), the cause of <s>dharma</s>, and the fruit of <s>dharma</s> are tenable. For him <s>adharma</s> (vice), the cause of <s>adharma</s>, and the fruit of <s>adharma</s> are tenable. For him the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the arising of <s>kleśas</s>, and the bases of <s>kleśas</s> are tenable. For whom all this previously stated [is tenable], for him the establishment of good destinies and bad destinies ... the going to good and bad destinies; the path leading to good and bad destinies; the transcendence of going to good and bad destinies; the means of transcending good and bad destinies; and all worldly conventional transactions [are tenable] — [these are] to be understood by oneself. In this direction, something can be taught by words.

body.text: bhavati cātra
body.translated_text: And here it is [said]:

body.text:
yaḥ śūnyatāṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ madhyamāṃ pratipadam
anekārthāṃ nijagāda praṇamāmi tam apratimaṃ tu buddhim iti ||
body.translated_text: He who taught <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and the Middle Path (<s>Madhyamā Pratipad</s>) as having manifold meanings — I bow to that incomparable wisdom [the Buddha].

body.text: kṛtir iyam ācāryanāgārjunapādānā + + + + + ekatra ślokaśata 450 ||
body.translated_text: This is the composition of the feet of <s>Āc��rya Nāgārjuna</s> ... one hundred verses in total, 450 [lines].

body.text: || likhitam idaṃ śrīdhramakirtinā sarvasatvahetoḥ yathālabdham iti ||
body.translated_text: This was copied by the illustrious <s>Dharmakīrti</s> for the sake of all beings, as obtained.

body.text: || vigrahavyāvartiṇī ||
body.translated_text: <s>Vigrahavyāvartanī</s> (The Turning Back of Disputes).
